pages.title: The Four Seasons
pages.summary: A band of travelers whose paths have become entwined with the fate of kingdoms, moonlight, and shadow.
pages.body:
# A name forged on the road
The **Four Seasons** is the name the adventurers chose in [[Kestrel Ford]], after surviving a far longer journey that began near [[Port Llast]]. Their story has crossed kingdoms, the sea, and even the [[Shadowfell]].

## The adventurers
The founding travelers were [[Bramwell Elixor]], [[Luna]], [[Bjorn]], and [[Fenwick]]. As the story grew, companions such as [[Amel]], [[Princess Yulia]], [[Brick]], and [[Estephan]] joined them along the road. [[Fenwick]] later departed the traveling party, though he remains part of its history.

## Friends, uneasy allies, and foes
The company's path has intertwined with [[Jimsko]], [[Flynn]], [[Velka]], and [[The Pirate Queen]]. New faces continue to appear as they travel, including [[Cinder]] in [[Thamor]].

## Follow their story
Explore the [[Campaign Chronicle]], open the **Session Journal** from the top navigation, or visit the **World Atlas** to trace their recorded journey.

> Four different paths. One story beneath the moon.

# A chronicle of the road
## Saga I — The daughter of the moon
Four travelers arrived in [[Port Llast]] and investigated the [[Port Llast Lighthouse]], then recovered the [[Moon Scroll]] in the [[Caverns of Lior]]. Their quest led them through [[Neverwinter]], [[Neverwinter Wood]], and [[Luskan]], where [[Jimsko]] was rescued and the mystery of the [[Moonfall Vault]] emerged.

Through the vault they entered the [[Shadowfell]] and traveled to [[Blackreach]], seeking a way back to the Material Plane. Their battle against the Unforgotten gave the [[Keeper]] time to open a [[Shadow Crossing]], and the adventurers returned to a wheat field beneath open sky.

Every Saga I session is recorded individually in the **Session Journal** (Sessions 1–17), based on the party's own recaps.

## Saga II — A name and a crown
The travelers reached [[Kestrel Ford]], where their company became [[The Four Seasons]]. After further travel they entered [[Thamor]], met [[Cinder]], and attended [[King Arven I]]'s knighting ceremony in [[Crown Square]]. There, an attempted attack disturbed the celebration and [[Bramwell Elixor]] blocked an incoming arrow.

*Only played events are recorded here. The next chapter is waiting to be written.*

pages.title: Bramwell Elixor
pages.summary: A human cleric of Helm whose convictions have drawn both admiration and controversy.
pages.body:
# The watchful hand
**Bramwell Elixor** is a human cleric devoted to [[Helm]]. A practiced alchemist as well as a priest, he has walked a difficult line between faith, responsibility, and what he believes to be right.

Bramwell became known for his efforts to help those afflicted by a terrible plague. That work, and the choices surrounding it, have complicated his relationship with religious authority.

## Travels
A founding member of [[The Four Seasons]], Bramwell has journeyed through [[Port Llast]], [[Neverwinter]], and [[Thamor]]. During the knighting ceremony in Thamor, he reacted to an arrow aimed into the gathering.

## Known connections
- [[Helm]] — god of guardians and vigilance
- [[The Four Seasons]] — his companions
- [[Luna]] and [[Bjorn]] — fellow adventurers

# A life written in questions
**Luna** travels with [[The Four Seasons]]. Mysterious dreams, unusual encounters, and the pull of the fey have followed her adventures.

Once known for her roguish talents, Luna's journey has taken her toward strange magic and a personal history that is not yet fully understood.

## On the road
Luna has traveled alongside [[Bramwell Elixor]] and [[Bjorn]] through [[Port Llast]], [[Neverwinter]], and the lands around [[Thamor]].

## A living entry
More of Luna's history will be added as it becomes part of the shared campaign story.

pages.title: Bjorn Bloodspiller
pages.summary: A towering goliath barbarian, formidable in battle and loyal to his companions.
pages.body:
# Björn Bloodspiller

*The Goliath Barbarian*

**Full name:** Björn Bloodspiller  

**Race:** Goliath  

**Class:** Barbarian  

**Gender:** Male  

**Affiliation:** Original Adventuring Party  

**Family:** Jimsko (father)  

**First appearance:** Saga I, Session 1  

**Last appearance:** Saga I, Session 6  

**Last known location:** Neverwinter Woods, near Neverwinter  

**Status:** Captured — current whereabouts unknown  

**Notable allies:** Bramwell Elixor, Luna Hale, Fenwick Elderbranch, Princess Yulia  

**Notable enemies:** Cultists of Shar, Velka (formerly), hostile pirates, and the forces pursuing Princess Yulia


---

## Overview

Björn Bloodspiller is a goliath barbarian and one of the four founding members of the adventuring party whose actions set the events of *The Daughter of the Moon* into motion.

Known for his immense physical strength, straightforward nature, impulsive decisions, and remarkable loyalty, Björn served as one of the party's primary frontline fighters during its earliest adventures along the Sword Coast.

The son of Jimsko, a dwarf residing in Port Llast, Björn became personally involved in the growing conflict surrounding an ancient prophetic scroll when his father was abducted by unknown assailants.

Throughout his travels, Björn demonstrated both an extraordinary talent for violence and a surprisingly earnest sense of duty. His adventures ranged from accidental tavern brawls and awkward romantic advances to confronting dangerous cultists and recovering an ancient magical artifact.

His defining moment came near Neverwinter, when he voluntarily confronted pursuers to protect Princess Yulia and allow his companions to escape.

Björn was subsequently captured, bringing his time with the adventuring party to an abrupt end.

His ultimate fate remains unknown.

## History

### Early Life

Little is currently known about Björn's childhood, upbringing, or life before becoming an adventurer.

He is the son of Jimsko, a dwarf living in the coastal settlement of Port Llast. The exact circumstances of their family relationship and Björn's upbringing have yet to be established.

Despite his father's relatively comfortable residence and connections within Port Llast, Björn chose a life of travel and adventure.

His physical prowess and preference for direct confrontation eventually led him to follow the path of a barbarian.

### Formation of the Adventuring Party

Björn's recorded adventures began on the road to Port Llast.

While traveling toward the coastal town, he encountered three other adventurers: Bramwell Elixor, a human cleric of Helm; Luna Hale, an elven rogue; and Fenwick Elderbranch, a gnome druid.

The four strangers discovered they were heading toward the same destination and agreed to travel together.

Their first journey was far from ordinary.

During a stop at a small cabin, Björn made an earnest romantic confession to its resident. Unfortunately, his advances were rejected, marking an awkward but memorable beginning to the party's travels.

Later, the group discovered a wrecked merchant wagon and were ambushed by a thief accompanied by two wolves.

The adventurers defeated their attackers and aided the merchant, proving themselves capable of working together despite their dramatically different personalities.

By the time they reached Port Llast, the four had already begun forming the bonds that would define the original party.

### Arrival in Port Llast

Upon arriving in Port Llast, the adventurers met Jimsko at the Net & Keg Tavern.

The dwarf welcomed them with generous hospitality, paying for their drinks as they enjoyed an evening of music and conversation.

During their stay, the party learned of unusual activity surrounding the town's lighthouse, whose supposedly automated beacon had begun behaving unpredictably.

The adventurers agreed to investigate.

Before beginning their mission, however, Björn and Bramwell staged a dramatic fight in the marketplace.

The confrontation was a deliberate distraction, allowing Luna to steal valuables from an unsuspecting merchant while everyone's attention remained fixed on the two brawlers.

The incident demonstrated an early aspect of Björn's personality: although often inclined toward physical confrontation, he was willing to participate in his companions' less conventional plans.

### The Lighthouse and the Memory Shard

As the party investigated Port Llast, Björn learned of a false lighthouse connected to suspicious maritime activity.

Their investigation led them into the mayor's residence and eventually to the town's true lighthouse.

There, the adventurers fought unnatural shades and uncovered the remains of an ancient shrine dedicated to Selûne.

At the lighthouse's summit, they confronted a bandit and two cultists attempting a mysterious ritual involving a magical shard.

The battle was chaotic, and Bramwell's clumsiness caused an unfortunate mishap at its beginning.

Nevertheless, the adventurers prevailed.

Following the confrontation, Björn touched the recovered shard and experienced a strange magical effect.

For several seconds, his memories vanished.

Though the effect was temporary, it provided the party with its first direct experience of the mysterious magic connected to the wider conflict.

Neither Björn nor his companions fully understood the artifact's nature, but the experience foreshadowed the central importance of memory throughout the saga.

### The Pirate Cove and the Caverns of Lior

Following their discovery at the lighthouse, the party reunited with Jimsko, who introduced them to Estephan, a small mouse companion possessing information about pirates and stolen scrolls.

The information led the adventurers to a hidden coastal encampment.

During their approach, Fenwick used his ability to transform into a rat to scout the location, while Björn and Bramwell opted for a considerably more direct investigation.

Predictably, the situation escalated into violence.

The adventurers defeated the pirates, destroyed their false lighthouse system, and discovered an entrance to the Caverns of Lior.

Within the caves, they rescued Flynn, a prisoner from Luskan, and confronted cultists guarding an ancient rune-covered stone barrier.

After overcoming the barrier, the party entered a chamber filled with strange blue magical energy.

At its center floated an ancient scroll.

As the party approached, Luna collapsed and began convulsing. While the other adventurers rushed to assist her, Björn retrieved the scroll from its pedestal.

He was among the first to examine the artifact and witness its strange magical countdown.

The numbers indicated that only three days remained before something significant would occur.

Although he could not understand the scroll's writing, Björn recognized its importance and the danger surrounding it.

The recovery of the scroll would transform the adventurers' journey from an investigation into a conflict involving ancient prophecies and divine powers.

### The Battle Against Velka

During their continued exploration of the caverns, the party encountered Velka, a woman associated with the cultist operation surrounding the scroll.

After negotiations failed, the encounter erupted into combat.

Björn proved instrumental in the battle.

His extraordinary strength and ability to withstand danger allowed him to keep fighting when his companions struggled.

Luna later described his performance as terrifying, recalling how he repeatedly struck enemies down and helped turn the tide whenever the party appeared close to defeat.

The adventurers eventually defeated Velka and took her prisoner.

The battle established Björn as one of the most formidable combatants among the original adventurers.

### The Abduction of Jimsko

After leaving the Caverns of Lior, the adventurers returned to Port Llast expecting a measure of safety.

Instead, they discovered that the inn had been attacked and Jimsko had disappeared.

Evidence suggested his captors had taken him north toward Luskan.

For Björn, the conflict was no longer simply a matter of protecting strangers or uncovering magical mysteries.

His father was missing.

Shortly afterward, the party encountered El, a representative of an order dedicated to Selûne.

She warned that the magical writing on the recovered scroll was disappearing and that the knowledge it contained might be lost unless the party reached Neverwinter.

Björn faced a painful choice.

He could pursue his father toward Luskan or accompany the party to Neverwinter and help preserve the knowledge contained in the scroll.

Ultimately, the group decided to travel to Neverwinter first.

El promised to use her connections to assist in locating Jimsko.

Although Björn continued the journey, his father's fate remained unresolved.

### The Journey to Neverwinter

The adventurers' journey toward Neverwinter brought further strange encounters.

Along the road, they discovered a murdered tiefling traveler carrying a cursed necklace capable of transforming its wearer into a chicken.

They also entered an enchanted forest inhabited by two mischievous fairies, Wiwi and Nini, who challenged the party with questions concerning Shar, Selûne, Mystra, and the origins of the Weave.

After successfully completing the challenge, the group received a blessing of heroic inspiration.

Upon arriving in Neverwinter, the adventurers began seeking information about the prophetic scroll.

Björn accompanied his companions to the Crown of Embers, a local tavern where an altercation rapidly escalated.

Together with Bramwell, he became involved in a full tavern-wide brawl.

The incident further reinforced his reputation as someone whose presence could turn an ordinary evening into complete chaos.

Despite the distractions, the adventurers made progress in their investigation.

At Neverwinter's library, a scholar helped decipher part of the ancient prophecy, revealing references to a forgotten moon and two daughters walking beneath divided skies.

The scroll's dangerous countdown was eventually broken, allowing the party to continue their investigation without the immediate threat of losing its contents.

### Meeting Princess Yulia

As the party prepared to depart Neverwinter, they encountered a group of guards escorting Princess Yulia.

Yulia was a rebellious young noblewoman who wanted freedom from the expectations and restrictions surrounding her royal position.

The adventurers intervened.

Using a smoke potion prepared by Bramwell, they helped Yulia escape her escort.

The princess subsequently asked to accompany them on their travels.

Björn immediately took on the responsibility of protecting her.

His willingness to defend the princess became one of his most defining commitments.

Despite his often reckless behavior, Björn regarded the promise seriously.

It was a decision that would soon carry considerable consequences.

### The Sacrifice in Neverwinter Woods

With Princess Yulia now traveling alongside them, the adventurers attempted to escape Neverwinter by traveling through the surrounding forests.

Their intention was to keep the princess hidden from those seeking her return.

Before they could disappear into the woods, El arrived accompanied by two guards.

The group faced the possibility of being discovered, captured, or forced to surrender the princess.

Björn chose to act.

Rather than remain concealed, he revealed himself and confronted the approaching pursuers.

His actions drew their attention away from his companions and the princess.

Although his considerable strength made him a dangerous opponent, Björn was eventually restrained and taken into custody.

His intervention gave the remaining adventurers the opportunity to flee deeper into the Neverwinter Woods.

The party escaped with Yulia, but Björn was left behind.

For Fenwick and the others, his capture was a painful loss.

Their companion had sacrificed his own freedom to uphold his promise.

### Disappearance

Following Björn's capture, the remaining adventurers continued their journey without him.

Deeper in the Neverwinter Woods, they encountered Amel, a rogue who subsequently joined the group.

Björn did not accompany the party to Luskan, where Jimsko was eventually found and rescued from the Pirate Queen's imprisonment.

He was also absent from the expedition to the Moonfall Vault and the later events of Saga I.

No confirmed account has yet established what happened to him after his capture near Neverwinter.

Whether he remains imprisoned, has been released, or has embarked on another adventure is unknown.

## Personality

Björn is best described as courageous, impulsive, loyal, and remarkably direct.

Unlike companions who prefer careful investigation, stealth, or diplomacy, Björn often favors decisive action and straightforward confrontation.

His immense physical power and willingness to throw himself into dangerous situations made him an effective frontline warrior, though his spontaneous decisions sometimes complicated the party's plans.

He also possesses a humorous and unexpectedly earnest side.

His unsuccessful romantic confession early in the campaign, participation in ridiculous distractions, and involvement in chaotic tavern incidents all demonstrate that he is far from a stern or humorless warrior.

Beneath these qualities lies a strong sense of responsibility toward those he cares about.

His concern for Jimsko and his commitment to Princess Yulia demonstrate that loyalty is among his most important traits.

When confronted with the choice between protecting himself and defending his companions, Björn proved willing to surrender his freedom for their safety.

## Abilities and Combat Style

### Physical Strength

As a goliath barbarian, Björn possesses exceptional physical strength and endurance.

His size and power make him particularly effective in close combat, where he can overpower opponents and absorb punishment that would overwhelm less resilient adventurers.

### Barbarian Rage

Björn follows the barbarian's path, employing his physical ferocity in battle.

His most notable display of combat prowess occurred during the confrontation with Velka, where he repeatedly helped keep the party alive against dangerous opposition.

### Frontline Protection

Although not necessarily a formally trained guardian, Björn frequently occupied the most dangerous positions in combat.

His ability to engage powerful enemies provided opportunities for his companions to employ magic, stealth, healing, and ranged attacks.

### Weapons

Björn has shown a preference for powerful melee weaponry and sought to acquire an axe during his time in Neverwinter.

His exact weapon inventory and magical equipment have not been fully documented.

## Relationships

### Jimsko — Father

Jimsko is Björn's father and one of his most important personal connections.

The dwarf's invitation brought the adventurers to Port Llast, where the campaign's central mysteries first began unfolding.

When Jimsko was abducted, Björn was forced to balance his concern for his father against the larger threat presented by the prophecy.

Their separation became one of the major emotional conflicts of Björn's journey.

Unfortunately, Björn was captured before the party eventually rescued Jimsko in Luskan.

### Bramwell Elixor — Companion

Bramwell and Björn formed an often chaotic partnership during the party's earliest adventures.

Together, they staged a fight in the Port Llast marketplace and later became involved in a tavern-wide brawl at the Crown of Embers.

Although their approaches occasionally lacked subtlety, the two proved capable of working together against dangerous enemies.

Bramwell's divine magic complemented Björn's physical fighting abilities.

### Luna Hale — Companion

Luna and Björn were founding members of the party.

Their contrasting methods frequently worked to their advantage: Luna favored stealth, deception, and opportunism, while Björn preferred direct action.

The staged marketplace fight provided an early example of their cooperation, with Björn serving as the distraction that allowed Luna to carry out a theft.

Luna also witnessed Björn's formidable performance in the Caverns of Lior and later recounted his fighting abilities with a mixture of admiration and humor.

### Fenwick Elderbranch — Companion

Fenwick and Björn traveled together from the beginning of the campaign.

Despite their vastly different sizes and approaches to problem-solving, they formed part of the original group that survived the dangers of Port Llast.

Following Björn's capture, Fenwick expressed regret at having to leave him behind.

His account of the incident emphasized the importance of Björn's sacrifice to the party's survival.

### Princess Yulia — Protected Ally

Princess Yulia became one of the most important individuals in Björn's final recorded adventures.

After helping free her from her escort in Neverwinter, Björn accepted the responsibility of protecting her.

He upheld this commitment even when confronted by El and armed guards.

His decision to expose himself and face capture allowed Yulia and the other adventurers to escape.

Their relationship remains one of the clearest examples of Björn's sense of duty.

### El — Pursuer

El initially appeared as an ally of the adventurers, offering assistance with the search for Jimsko and guidance concerning the prophetic scroll.

However, her interests eventually conflicted with the party's decision to travel with Princess Yulia.

When she arrived with guards near Neverwinter, Björn confronted them in an effort to protect the princess.

This confrontation led directly to his capture.

### Velka — Former Enemy

Björn fought Velka during the party's exploration of the Caverns of Lior.

The confrontation was one of his most significant early battles, demonstrating his strength and importance to the group's survival.

Following her defeat, Velka became the party's prisoner and an important source of information about Shar's followers.

## Notable Events and Achievements

- Founding member of the original adventuring party.
- Survived the first roadside ambush involving a thief and two wolves.
- Helped stage the Port Llast marketplace brawl.
- Participated in the investigation of the corrupted lighthouse.
- Experienced temporary memory loss after touching the mysterious shard.
- Helped defeat pirates and cultists in the Caverns of Lior.
- Personally retrieved the ancient prophetic scroll from its magical pedestal.
- Played a decisive role in the battle against Velka.
- Helped protect the party during its journey toward Neverwinter.
- Participated in the notorious Crown of Embers tavern brawl.
- Took responsibility for protecting Princess Yulia.
- Sacrificed his freedom to allow his companions and the princess to escape.

## Trivia

- Björn was one of the four original adventurers whose journey began on the road to Port Llast.
- He is a goliath, although his known father, Jimsko, is a dwarf.
- He was temporarily affected by memory-altering magic before the party fully understood its significance.
- He once chose to sleep beside barrels at the inn rather than in a conventional bed.
- His early romantic advances at a roadside cabin were unsuccessful.
- He and Bramwell were responsible for more than one memorable public disturbance.
- He was the adventurer who physically recovered the prophetic scroll from the pedestal in the caverns.
- His capture occurred before Jimsko's eventual rescue in Luskan.
- He was succeeded in the active party by Amel, whom the remaining adventurers encountered shortly afterward.

## Legacy

Björn Bloodspiller's adventures ended far sooner than those of many of his companions, yet his influence upon the party remained significant.

As one of the founding adventurers, he helped establish the unlikely alliance that would eventually become involved in the conflict between Selûne and Shar.

His strength was essential during the earliest battles, and his actions helped the party recover the prophetic scroll that lay at the center of the unfolding mystery.

Yet his greatest contribution was not a victory won through strength.

It was a promise kept.

When Princess Yulia faced capture, Björn chose to stand against her pursuers, knowing that doing so could cost him his freedom.

The adventurers continued their journey because he remained behind.

His story, therefore, stands as a reminder that heroism is not measured solely by enemies defeated or treasures recovered, but also by the sacrifices made for others.

**The fate of Björn Bloodspiller remains an unwritten chapter in the history of the Sword Coast.**

pages.title: Fenwick
pages.summary: A gnome druid, also known as Xero, who once traveled with the company.
pages.body:
# Fenwick Elderbranch

*The Druid Who Walked Through Shadow*

**Full name:** Fenwick Elderbranch  

**Race:** Gnome  

**Class:** Druid (with an evolving connection to shadow)  

**Affiliation:** The Original Adventuring Party; The Four Seasons  

**First appearance:** Saga I, Session 1  

**Status:** Alive  

**Current location:** Thamor  

**Former locations:** Port Llast, Neverwinter, Luskan, Moonfall Vault, Blackreach  

**Notable companions:** Bramwell Elixor, Luna Hale, Björn Bloodspiller, Amel, Veren
  
**Notable equipment:** Serpent-shaped druidic staff
  
**Associated powers:** Wild Shape, druidic magic, animal communication, nature magic

---

## Overview

Fenwick Elderbranch is a gnome druid, one of the four founding members of the adventuring party at the heart of *The Daughter of the Moon*, and a survivor of the Shadowfell.

Thoughtful, compassionate, inquisitive, and occasionally eccentric, Fenwick has often served as a voice of empathy and reason among companions whose solutions to problems tend to involve considerable violence, questionable deception, or both.

His affinity for animals and the natural world distinguishes him from the party's other adventurers. Where others see monsters, Fenwick frequently sees creatures acting according to instinct, fear, or the need to survive.

Despite his small stature, Fenwick has proven to be a resourceful combatant, capable investigator, and valuable ally. Through druidic magic and his ability to assume animal forms, he has helped his companions infiltrate enemy strongholds, overcome dangerous opponents, and survive hostile environments.

His adventures have taken him from the peaceful forests of the Sword Coast to the unnatural depths of the Moonfall Vault and the memory-haunted city of Blackreach.

His experiences in the Shadowfell profoundly affected his understanding of nature. After returning to the Material Plane, Fenwick began to sense something unfamiliar within the darkness, suggesting that his connection to the natural world might be changing.

## History

### Early Life

Little is currently known about Fenwick's life before joining the adventuring party.

His origins, family history, and the circumstances of his druidic training have not yet been fully revealed.

However, his actions demonstrate a deep understanding of the natural world, a willingness to show mercy to animals, and an instinctive curiosity toward unfamiliar forms of life and magic.

Unlike many adventurers who regard dangerous creatures as obstacles to be destroyed, Fenwick has repeatedly demonstrated that compassion can be just as useful as force.

### Formation of the Adventuring Party

Fenwick's recorded adventures began along the road to Port Llast.

While traveling toward the coastal settlement, he encountered three strangers heading in the same direction: Bramwell Elixor, a cleric of Helm; Luna Hale, an elven rogue; and Björn Bloodspiller, a goliath barbarian.

The four agreed to travel together.

Their first journey brought them into conflict with a thief accompanied by two wolves near a wrecked merchant wagon.

After defeating their attackers, Fenwick noticed that one of the wolves had survived.

Rather than kill the wounded animal, he approached it carefully, calmed it, and tended to its injuries before allowing it to return to the wilderness.

This encounter became an early demonstration of the principles guiding his actions.

Although the wolf had attacked the party, Fenwick recognized that it was still a living creature deserving of compassion.

The incident established a recurring theme throughout his adventures: Fenwick's belief that nature should be understood rather than needlessly harmed.

### The Mysteries of Port Llast

Upon reaching Port Llast, Fenwick and his companions met Jimsko, a dwarven resident who had invited the adventurers to investigate disturbances surrounding the town's lighthouse.

Their investigation led them into an increasingly complex mystery involving corrupt officials, suspicious maritime activity, ancient religious ruins, and cultists.

Fenwick accompanied the party during its investigation of the mayor's residence, where they discovered unusual paintings, documents, and a book associated with Selûne.

The party subsequently explored the lighthouse itself, uncovering a forgotten shrine beneath its foundations and confronting cultists at its summit.

During the confrontation, the adventurers recovered a mysterious magical shard capable of temporarily affecting memories.

This discovery provided their first glimpse into the strange forces at work behind the events unfolding around Port Llast.

### The Pirate Cove and Caverns of Lior

Following the lighthouse investigation, Jimsko introduced the party to Estephan, who possessed information concerning pirates and stolen scrolls.

The adventurers followed the clues toward a hidden coastal encampment.

While the others debated their approach, Fenwick transformed into a rat and used his small animal form to scout the pirate camp.

His ability to infiltrate dangerous locations unnoticed proved particularly valuable, providing the group with information before the inevitable confrontation.

After defeating the pirates and destroying their false lighthouse system, the party entered the Caverns of Lior.

During their exploration, Fenwick frequently adopted the form of a wolf.

His transformed state allowed him to fight alongside his companions while employing the natural instincts and physical abilities of a predator.

The party eventually encountered Velka, a woman associated with the operation surrounding an ancient prophetic scroll.

Following a difficult battle, the adventurers defeated her and took her prisoner.

The discoveries inside the caverns revealed that the group had become involved in a mystery far greater than a simple pirate operation.

### Journey to Neverwinter

After discovering that Jimsko had been abducted, the adventurers traveled toward Neverwinter to investigate the magical scroll they had recovered.

On their journey, Fenwick encountered unusual magical creatures and phenomena, including the fairies Wiwi and Nini, who challenged the party with questions about the gods and the history of the Weave.

Upon arriving in Neverwinter, Fenwick showed particular interest in the city's scholarly resources.

While other companions spent their evening at the Crown of Embers tavern, Fenwick visited the Wizard's Rest.

The following day, he encouraged the party to seek information about ancient Netherese lore at the city's library.

His curiosity proved valuable.

The party succeeded in obtaining a partial translation of the prophecy, which contained references to the sea forgetting the moon and two daughters walking beneath divided skies.

The discovery helped them understand the significance of the scroll and break its dangerous magical countdown.

### The Capture of Björn

As the party departed Neverwinter with Princess Yulia, they attempted to avoid attention by traveling through the surrounding forests.

Their plans were interrupted when El arrived with two guards, seeking to confront the group.

Björn chose to reveal himself and face the pursuers, allowing the others to escape with the princess.

He was restrained and taken away.

Fenwick was deeply affected by the loss of his companion.

Although Björn's sacrifice allowed the party to continue its journey, Fenwick struggled with the decision to leave him behind.

It was one of the first major separations suffered by the original group.

### The Hidden Druid Sanctuary

Deep within the Neverwinter Woods, the adventurers encountered the wandering storyteller Volo, who spoke of a hidden druidic sanctuary.

Fenwick became particularly interested in the possibility of discovering a place dedicated to the natural world.

After following clues involving a statue of Silvanus, an unusual crow, and an ancient forest path, the party discovered a cave marked with a druidic inscription.

The passage led through chambers filled with glowing crystals, giant spiders, and eventually an owlbear guarding a sealed stone door.

The situation escalated when Bramwell's attack accidentally destroyed the owlbear's egg, causing the creature to fly into a rage.

The resulting confrontation ended in the guardian's death.

However, Fenwick had refused to harm the owlbear.

After the battle, he discovered an inscription upon the door:

*Hurt not the Guardian and you shall pass.*

Because Fenwick had not attacked the creature, the door opened at his touch.

Beyond it lay a staircase leading into the hidden druid sanctuary.

The sanctuary recognized the restraint that Fenwick had shown even when faced with a dangerous beast.

His encounter with the druids also rewarded him with a distinctive serpent-shaped staff, becoming one of his notable possessions.

The experience reinforced the importance of mercy and respect for nature in Fenwick's journey.

### The City of Luskan

Following their journey through the Neverwinter Woods, the party arrived in Luskan.

By this point, reports of their involvement in Princess Yulia's disappearance had spread, and many of the adventurers were wanted criminals.

The group attempted to avoid unwanted attention while searching for information concerning Jimsko.

Fenwick participated in their investigations and accompanied the others to a theatrical performance dramatizing their own adventures.

During the performance, the group reunited with Flynn, a prisoner they had previously rescued from the Caverns of Lior.

Flynn provided assistance as the party became increasingly entangled in the schemes of the Pirate Queen of the North.

### The Rescue of Jimsko and Velka

The adventurers eventually discovered that Jimsko and Velka were imprisoned within one of the Pirate Queen's Ledger Houses.

To investigate the building, Fenwick used his Wild Shape ability to become a cat.

His infiltration was briefly complicated by an encounter with another cat, who appeared to be defending her young.

Rather than provoke a fight, Fenwick avoided harming the animal and rejoined his companions.

The party devised an elaborate escape plan involving stealth, magic, and the manipulation of the surrounding earth.

Luna located the prisoners and unlocked their cell, while Bramwell helped create an escape route through the structure.

The group successfully freed Jimsko and Velka.

Following their rescue, Jimsko revealed information about an ancient underwater location known as the Moonfall Vault.

This discovery gave the adventurers their next destination.

### The Moonfall Vault

Fenwick accompanied the party on its expedition toward the Moonfall Vault.

Their journey took them to a ruined island containing an ancient moon pool dedicated to Selûne.

When the moon rose, a ritual activated the pool and opened a passage into an extraordinary underwater complex.

Within the submerged ruins, the adventurers discovered ancient structures, magical creatures, sunken ships, and an unusually large population of hostile crabs.

Fenwick attempted to communicate with the smaller crabs.

Unfortunately, their intentions were far from friendly.

Through his magic, he learned that the creatures wished to kill the adventurers and bring their bodies before the monstrous Crab Queen.

The encounter demonstrated that Fenwick's ability to communicate with animals did not necessarily guarantee cooperation.

The party eventually defeated the Crab Queen and recovered the magical orb needed to activate another ancient structure.

However, their victory was short-lived.

A terrifying elder lich partially emerged from a corrupted statue of Selûne and unleashed a powerful spell.

The magic tore the adventurers away from the Material Plane and cast them into the Shadowfell.

### The Shadowfell

The Shadowfell proved unlike anything Fenwick had previously experienced.

The natural beauty and vitality of the world he understood had been replaced by black grass, colorless landscapes, unnatural silence, and an overwhelming sense of loss.

For a druid whose abilities and identity were closely connected to the living world, the experience was profoundly unsettling.

The adventurers eventually reached Blackreach, a strange city where memories could be exchanged, stolen, and forgotten.

As they searched for a way home, Fenwick began documenting the group's discoveries.

He became particularly interested in the mysterious Shadow Crossings, passages capable of connecting the Shadowfell to the Material Plane.

### The Eye of Memories

While investigating Blackreach, Fenwick helped decipher mysterious runes that had appeared through Luna's magical dagger.

One word proved particularly important: Keeper.

Believing that the message might provide a way out of the Shadowfell, Fenwick accompanied the party to the city's library.

There, they discovered that Shar had destroyed the known Shadow Crossings and learned of an ancient entity known as the Keeper, supposedly hidden beneath the city.

The Keeper was believed to possess knowledge of the last remaining crossing.

During their journey through Blackreach, Fenwick noticed something extraordinary.

A tiny green plant had appeared between the stones of the city.

It seemed alive, healthy, and completely out of place in the lifeless landscape.

When he looked again, it had vanished.

Fenwick could not determine whether the plant had truly existed or whether the Shadowfell was beginning to affect his mind.

Nevertheless, the encounter gave him hope.

Even in a place defined by memory, darkness, and decay, he desperately wanted to believe that life could still take root.

### Annabel and the Keeper

The adventurers eventually discovered Annabel, a mysterious young girl connected to a missing memory.

While some of the party pursued a confrontation with the Black Knight, Fenwick remained with Luna, Annabel, and their companions to investigate the child's connection to the Keeper.

The party learned that Annabel could guide them toward the entity they had been searching for.

They subsequently helped reunite her with her mother, Ariana, whose memories of her daughter had been lost.

Although the reunion proved temporary, it allowed Annabel to experience one final moment of recognition and affection.

In return, she guided the adventurers into Blackreach's Forgotten District, where the Keeper awaited.

### The Battle Against the Unforgotten

The Keeper offered the adventurers a chance to escape the Shadowfell by opening a Shadow Crossing.

However, activating the passage would attract powerful entities determined to prevent the ritual.

The party agreed to defend the Keeper.

As the ritual began, a monstrous creature known as the Unforgotten emerged from the darkness.

The being attacked not only the adventurers' bodies but also their memories, forcing them to confront fragments of their past.

Fenwick fought alongside Bramwell, Luna, Amel, and Veren during the desperate battle.

Together, they protected the Keeper long enough for the ritual to be completed.

The Unforgotten was defeated, and the Shadow Crossing opened.

The adventurers escaped.

When they regained consciousness, they found themselves lying in a wheat field beneath an open sky.

They had finally returned to the Material Plane.

### Saga II — The Four Seasons

Following their escape from the Shadowfell, Fenwick and his surviving companions found themselves in unfamiliar territory, far from the Sword Coast.

The group eventually adopted the name **The Four Seasons**, marking a new chapter in their adventures.

Their travels took them through Kestrel Ford and onward toward the city of Thamor.

However, Fenwick's experiences in the Shadowfell had left a lasting impression.

His connection to nature no longer felt quite the same as it once had.

The natural world remained familiar, but there was now something else beneath its surface: an awareness of shadows, darkness, and the harsher instincts of survival.

During the party's journey toward Thamor, this changing relationship with nature became a significant part of Fenwick's personal story.

Whether these developments represent a new form of druidic understanding or the beginning of an entirely different path remains an open question.

## Personality

Fenwick is thoughtful, compassionate, curious, and often surprisingly humorous.

He possesses a genuine affection for animals and an interest in understanding creatures that others might simply regard as dangerous.

His mercy toward the wounded wolf and the owlbear guardian illustrate his respect for living things, even under difficult circumstances.

Unlike Björn's preference for direct confrontation or Luna's inclination toward deception, Fenwick frequently approaches problems through observation, investigation, or creative uses of magic.

He is also an enthusiastic learner.

His visits to libraries, interest in druidic sanctuaries, and careful documentation of events in Blackreach demonstrate an intellectual curiosity extending well beyond his immediate responsibilities.

Despite his gentle nature, Fenwick is not incapable of violence. When necessary, he willingly fights to defend his companions.

His humor often appears in unexpected situations, particularly when recounting encounters with dangerous creatures or unreasonable people.

Beneath this lightheartedness lies a persistent determination to protect life and preserve hope.

## Abilities and Powers

### Wild Shape

Fenwick possesses the druidic ability to transform into animals.

His known transformations include:

- **Rat:** Used to infiltrate and scout the pirate encampment near Port Llast.
- **Wolf:** Used during exploration and combat within the Caverns of Lior.
- **Cat:** Used while infiltrating the Pirate Queen's Ledger House in Luskan.

His transformations provide a combination of stealth, mobility, reconnaissance, and combat versatility.

### Animal Communication

Fenwick can communicate with animals through druidic magic.

This ability has allowed him to understand creatures that would otherwise be impossible to question, including the hostile crabs encountered within the Moonfall Vault.

### Nature Magic

As a druid, Fenwick draws upon the natural world for his magic.

His abilities allow him to interact with animals, adapt to different environments, and assist his companions through magical and practical knowledge.

### Shadow Awareness

Following his experiences in Blackreach, Fenwick began developing an unfamiliar sensitivity to darkness.

The Shadowfell appears to have altered how he perceives the natural world, introducing a connection to the instincts of concealment, hunting, and survival.

The nature and full extent of this change remain uncertain.

## Notable Equipment

### Serpent-Shaped Staff

A distinctive druidic staff acquired during Fenwick's visit to the hidden sanctuary within Neverwinter Woods.

The staff symbolizes his connection to the natural world and his successful passage through the sanctuary's trial.

Its full magical properties have not yet been documented.

## Relationships

### Bramwell Elixor

Bramwell and Fenwick are founding members of the party.

Although the cleric's impulsive decisions and occasional recklessness have complicated their adventures, the two have repeatedly fought alongside one another.

Their differing approaches to faith, nature, and danger create an interesting contrast.

### Luna Hale

Luna and Fenwick have traveled together since the party's formation.

Both possess considerable abilities in stealth and infiltration, though they employ different methods.

Within Blackreach, the two worked together to decipher the runes associated with the Keeper and investigate the mysteries surrounding Annabel.

Their partnership demonstrates how Fenwick's investigative curiosity complements Luna's resourcefulness.

### Björn Bloodspiller

Björn was one of Fenwick's original companions.

The goliath's strength made him a valuable protector during their early battles.

Although their personalities and approaches to danger differed considerably, Fenwick regarded him as a friend.

Björn's capture near Neverwinter affected Fenwick deeply, particularly because the party was forced to continue without him.

### Amel

Amel joined the adventurers after they encountered him within the Neverwinter Woods.

His pragmatic, occasionally cynical outlook contrasts with Fenwick's compassion and affinity for nature.

Nevertheless, the two survived the dangers of Luskan, the Moonfall Vault, and the Shadowfell together.

### Veren

Veren became a companion during the later stages of Saga I.

He fought alongside Fenwick and the others during the final confrontation against the Unforgotten.

Together, they escaped the Shadowfell and returned to the Material Plane.

### Brick

Brick, the party's crab companion, represents one of the more unusual creatures to accompany the adventurers.

Given Fenwick's affinity for animals, Brick naturally occupies an interesting place among the group's companions.

The two experienced several strange events together, including the increasing presence of supernatural forces during the party's travels.

## Notable Achievements

- Helped establish the original adventuring party.
- Spared and healed a wounded wolf during the party's first journey.
- Investigated the mysteries surrounding Port Llast.
- Used Wild Shape to infiltrate a pirate encampment.
- Helped defeat Velka in the Caverns of Lior.
- Encouraged the investigation of Netherese writings in Neverwinter.
- Gained entry to a hidden druid sanctuary without harming its owlbear guardian.
- Acquired a distinctive serpent-shaped staff.
- Infiltrated a Ledger House in the form of a cat.
- Helped rescue Jimsko and Velka from captivity.
- Communicated with hostile crabs in the Moonfall Vault.
- Survived transportation into the Shadowfell.
- Helped investigate Blackreach and the Eye of Memories.
- Assisted in discovering the existence of the Keeper.
- Helped Annabel find her mother.
- Fought against the Unforgotten.
- Escaped the Shadowfell with his companions.
- Became a founding member of the Four Seasons.

## Trivia

- Fenwick was one of the four original player characters at the beginning of the campaign.
- He has transformed into a rat, wolf, and cat during recorded adventures.
- He once avoided a potentially dangerous confrontation with another cat while infiltrating an enemy building.
- He was the only party member able to open the sanctuary door through his refusal to attack the owlbear guardian.
- His ability to speak with animals revealed that the crabs in the Moonfall Vault had murderous intentions.
- He kept a journal documenting events within Blackreach.
- The appearance of a tiny green plant in the Shadowfell became a particularly meaningful experience for him.
- He was among the five adventurers who survived the battle against the Unforgotten.
- His experiences in the Shadowfell continue to influence his understanding of nature.

## Legacy

Fenwick Elderbranch has survived places where the natural order itself seems broken.

From the forests of the Sword Coast to the unnatural depths of Blackreach, his journey has repeatedly challenged the principles that define him.

He has witnessed violence, betrayal, divine mysteries, unnatural creatures, and the destruction of memories.

Yet throughout his adventures, Fenwick has continued to search for understanding.

His compassion toward animals, curiosity about ancient magic, and determination to preserve life have made him an important part of the adventuring party.

The Shadowfell, however, has changed him.

Having witnessed a world where darkness seems capable of consuming everything, Fenwick now faces a new question.

Is darkness truly separate from nature, or has it always been part of the same cycle?

For a druid who once found hope in a wounded wolf and a solitary green plant, the answer may change his understanding of the world forever.

**Fenwick's story continues in Saga II: The Four Seasons.**

pages.title: Jimsko
pages.summary: The Dwarf of Port Llast
pages.body:
**Race:** Dwarf  

**Also known as:** Jimmy, Jimmy Jim  

**Residence:** Port Llast, Sword Coast  

**Affiliation:** Allies of the adventuring party  

**Family:** [[Bjorn|Björn Bloodpiller]] (son) 

**First appearance:** Saga I, Session 1  

**Status:** Alive — rescued from captivity  

**Notable possessions:** Journal, Bag of Holding  

**Associated locations:** Port Llast, Luskan, Moonfall Vault

---

## Overview

Jimsko, affectionately known as Jimmy, is a dwarven resident of Port Llast and one of the earliest allies of the adventuring party. A generous host, a concerned observer of the strange happenings along the northern Sword Coast, and a man possessing knowledge far more valuable than he initially revealed, Jimsko played an instrumental role in setting the events of *The Daughter of the Moon* into motion.

He is the father of Björn Bloodpiller, the party's goliath barbarian, and was the original contact who brought the adventurers together in Port Llast.

Although he initially appeared to be an ordinary, hospitable dwarf concerned about his town's malfunctioning lighthouse, later events revealed that Jimsko possessed important information concerning an ancient underwater location known as the Moonfall Vault.

His knowledge eventually made him a target of the Pirate Queen of the North.

## History

### The Invitation to Port Llast

Before the adventurers' arrival, Jimsko had become increasingly troubled by unusual activity around Port Llast.

Of particular concern was the town's supposedly automated lighthouse, whose beacon had begun flickering unpredictably. Suspecting that something was wrong, Jimsko invited the adventurers to Port Llast to investigate.

The party arrived after traveling together along the Sword Coast, encountering danger before they even reached their destination.

They found Jimsko enjoying himself at the local inn, the Net & Keg Tavern. He welcomed the travelers warmly, providing drinks and hospitality at his own expense.

That evening, amid music, conversation, and considerable drinking, the group learned of the troubling lighthouse rumors. They agreed to investigate the matter as a favor to Jimmy.

What began as a seemingly simple request would lead the party toward pirates, secret cults, ancient Netherese writings, and a prophecy involving two daughters of opposing divine powers.

### The Lighthouse Investigation

The adventurers' investigation uncovered evidence of suspicious activity surrounding Port Llast's harbor, its mayor, and the lighthouse itself.

Beneath the lighthouse, the party discovered the remains of an ancient shrine dedicated to Selûne. An empty space suggested that an important object had recently been removed.

At the lighthouse's summit, the adventurers confronted a bandit and two cultists performing a mysterious ritual involving a magical shard.

The discovery confirmed that Jimsko's concerns were justified. Something far more dangerous than a failing lighthouse was unfolding around Port Llast.

### Estephan and the Pirate Cove

Following the lighthouse investigation, Jimsko introduced the adventurers to Estephan, a small mouse companion who had gathered intelligence about suspicious activity near a coastal cove.

Estephan's information connected the activities of local pirates to stolen scrolls and a concealed camp.

Following these leads, the party discovered a pirate encampment, a false lighthouse system, and the entrance to the Caverns of Lior.

Deep within the caverns, they eventually recovered an ancient magical scroll carrying an ominous countdown.

The scroll would become central to the unfolding prophecy and the conflict between the followers of Selûne and Shar.

### The Abduction of Jimsko

When the adventurers returned to Port Llast following their confrontation with Velka in the Caverns of Lior, they discovered that the inn had been attacked.

Jimsko had disappeared.

Evidence suggested that his captors had taken him north toward Luskan, the dangerous City of Sails.

For Björn, the disappearance presented a deeply personal crisis. His father was missing, possibly in the hands of dangerous enemies, while the ancient scroll the party had recovered appeared to be losing its magical writing.

The adventurers faced a difficult decision: pursue Jimsko immediately or travel to Neverwinter in hopes of preserving the prophecy before its secrets vanished.

They ultimately chose Neverwinter.

El, a representative of an order devoted to Selûne, promised to use her contacts to help locate Jimsko while the party continued investigating the scroll.

### Captivity in Luskan

The party's search eventually led them into the dangerous political world of Luskan and the influence of the Pirate Queen of the North.

During an audience with the Queen, the adventurers were offered a bargain involving the removal of Shar's cultists from the city. Jimsko's release was among the promised rewards.

However, the Queen's motivations were far from charitable.

Jimsko possessed information she desperately wanted, information connected to the ancient scroll and the investigations undertaken by Velka.

He had refused to surrender this knowledge willingly.

Ultimately, the party discovered him imprisoned alongside Velka inside one of the Queen's so-called Ledger Houses, a false tax office used to conceal darker operations.

Luna infiltrated the building and unlocked the prisoners' cell. With Bramwell's help, the adventurers created an escape route through the building and fled with both captives.

Jimsko was finally reunited with his son and the party.

### The Secret of the Moonfall Vault

Following the rescue, the adventurers returned to Flynn's safehouse in Luskan.

There, Jimsko revealed why he had been taken prisoner.

He knew of the **Moonfall Vault**, a hidden ancient location deep beneath the sea, connected to the mysteries of the scroll.

This knowledge explained the Pirate Queen's determination to capture him.

Jimsko's revelation, together with Velka's translation of the prophecy, provided the party with a new direction.

Unfortunately, the Queen had anticipated his refusal to cooperate. Rather than forcing the information from him, she allowed the adventurers to lead her toward it.

Through a magical projection, she revealed that she had deliberately manipulated the situation, expecting Jimsko to share his secrets once freed.

With her knowledge of the Moonfall Vault now growing, the race to reach the ancient site had begun.

### Return to Port Llast

Following their escape from Luskan, the group arranged passage aboard a ship obtained through Flynn's connections.

The vessel returned first to Port Llast, where Jimsko visited his home and gathered his belongings before the expedition continued.

His residence was notably spacious and well maintained, with possessions that included a journal and a Bag of Holding.

The party also prepared for the dangers ahead, obtaining new clothing and equipment suitable for their intended journey.

Velka, Princess Yulia, and Vesper remained behind to pursue investigations on land while the expedition departed toward the mysterious Moonfall Vault.

## Personality

Jimsko's actions reveal a hospitable, practical, and determined individual.

He is generous with those he trusts, demonstrated by his willingness to welcome the adventurers and cover their expenses during their first evening in Port Llast.

His concern over the lighthouse shows an observant nature and an unwillingness to ignore suspicious events, even when the threat is not yet understood.

Despite falling into the hands of one of the North's most dangerous pirate rulers, Jimsko refused to willingly reveal the secrets she sought.

He appears to understand that certain knowledge can become dangerous in the wrong hands.

## Relationships

### Björn Bloodpiller

Björn is Jimsko's son and a member of the adventuring party.

Their relationship became central to the party's early journey when Jimsko was abducted.

Björn was forced to weigh his desire to rescue his father against the urgency of preserving the ancient prophecy. The eventual rescue in Luskan brought an end to that period of uncertainty.

### The Adventuring Party

Jimsko was responsible for bringing the original adventurers to Port Llast.

His request concerning the lighthouse became their first major undertaking together, establishing a relationship that would continue throughout Saga I.

Over time, the party's involvement shifted from assisting a concerned local resident to rescuing a valued ally and relying upon his knowledge.

### Estephan

Jimsko introduced Estephan to the party during their time in Port Llast.

The small mouse possessed valuable intelligence about pirate activity and stolen scrolls, helping guide the adventurers toward the coast and the Caverns of Lior.

### Velka

Jimsko and Velka became connected through the mysteries surrounding the prophetic scroll and the Moonfall Vault.

Both were imprisoned within the Queen's Ledger House in Luskan, and both were rescued during the same infiltration.

Following their escape, their combined knowledge helped the party uncover more of the prophecy.

### The Pirate Queen of the North

The Pirate Queen regarded Jimsko as a valuable source of information.

She sought his knowledge of the Moonfall Vault and held him prisoner after he refused to cooperate.

Her calculated manipulation of his rescue demonstrated that she understood his loyalties well enough to exploit them.

The two remain opposed in their pursuit and protection of the Vault's secrets.

## Possessions and Residence

Jimsko owns a comfortable and well-kept residence in Port Llast, considerably more impressive than one might initially expect from his unassuming introduction.

Among his known possessions are a personal journal and a Bag of Holding.

His journal and knowledge are associated with his investigation of the Moonfall Vault, although its precise contents have not been fully established.

## Legacy and Significance

Few individuals have influenced the beginnings of the adventurers' journey as profoundly as Jimsko.

Without his invitation, the party may never have investigated the lighthouse, uncovered the cult's activities in Port Llast, or followed the trail that led to the ancient prophecy.

His abduction also transformed the growing conflict into something deeply personal for Björn and his companions.

Ultimately, Jimsko's knowledge helped connect the seemingly unrelated mysteries of Port Llast, Luskan, the stolen scroll, and the Moonfall Vault.

What began with a dwarf buying drinks for four travelers became part of a struggle involving ancient magic, divine prophecy, and the fate of the Sword Coast.

pages.title: Princess Yulia
pages.summary: A spirited princess of Neverwinter with silver hair and striking moonlike eyes.
pages.body:
# The princess of Neverwinter
**Princess Yulia** is a member of the royal family of [[Neverwinter]]. Her silver hair and moonlike eyes have made her memorable to those who have met her.

Despite royal expectations, Yulia is known for her lively spirit, willingness to speak her mind, and concern for the people beyond the palace walls.

Her story has begun to intersect with that of [[The Four Seasons]].

pages.title: King Arven I
pages.summary: The young king of Thamor, trying to wear a crown in an uncertain age.
pages.body:
# A young crown
**King Arven I** rules [[Thamor]] at an age when most children are still discovering who they wish to become.

The king presided over a much-anticipated knighting ceremony in [[Crown Square]], attended by guards, residents, and visiting dignitaries. An attempted attack disrupted the festivities.

## A contested future
Thamor faces outside pressure from [[Mourktar]], while the ominous [[Dragon's Due]] weighs on public conversation. With a child on the throne, every public appearance carries political weight.

pages.title: Grath Erlkar
pages.summary: A veteran leader and first captain associated with Port Llast.
pages.body:
# Grath Erlkar

*The First Captain of Port Llast*

**Full name:** Grath Erlkar  
**Race:** Human  
**Age:** 58  
**Gender:** Male  
**Occupation:** First Captain of Port Llast  
**Former occupation:** Pirate, sailor  
**Affiliation:** Port Llast  
**Residence:** First Captain's Residence, Port Llast  
**First appearance:** Saga I, Session 2  
**Status:** Alive  
**Known associations:** Port Llast's maritime community; former pirate connections  
**Notable possessions:** Lighthouse keys, maritime charts, old correspondence, sea-pointing compass, pirate relics  
**Alignment:** Not formally established

---

## Overview

Grath Erlkar is the First Captain of Port Llast, serving as the coastal settlement's primary political authority and protector.

A former pirate whose life has been shaped by decades at sea, Grath is a stern, experienced, and respected figure among the town's inhabitants. His position was not inherited or purchased; it was earned through his involvement in the liberation of Port Llast from pirate occupation thirty-five years before the events of *The Daughter of the Moon*.

Despite his reputation as a capable leader, Grath remains a guarded individual who rarely discusses his earlier life. His years upon the Sea of Swords left him with powerful connections, painful memories, and personal affairs that have never been fully resolved.

During the adventurers' investigation into the strange activities surrounding Port Llast's lighthouse, Grath became an object of suspicion.

His unusual behavior, possession of lighthouse keys, collection of maritime documents, and mysterious correspondence suggested that he was withholding information.

However, the discoveries within his residence pointed toward a complicated personal history rather than proving his involvement in the cultist conspiracy.

Grath is not a follower of Shar, nor was he established as the mastermind behind the lighthouse operation.

His greatest secrets appear to belong to his life before becoming First Captain.

## Appearance

Grath is an older human man whose appearance reflects a lifetime spent aboard ships and along the harsh northern coastline.

His stern expression and weathered features give him the presence of someone accustomed to command.

He carries himself with the authority of a veteran sailor rather than the refinement of a traditional noble.

Although now responsible for governing a settlement, he retains the bearing of a man who once lived by the dangers and uncertainties of the sea.

His appearance and mannerisms make it clear that he is no stranger to hardship.

## History

### Life Before Port Llast

Before becoming First Captain, Grath lived the dangerous life of a pirate.

His early years were spent sailing the Sea of Swords, navigating the complex world of maritime trade, piracy, and the rival powers competing for control of the northern coast.

Little is known about the precise circumstances of his time at sea.

However, his experiences left him with considerable knowledge of navigation, shipping routes, seafaring traditions, and the individuals who operate beyond the authority of coastal settlements.

His past also brought him into contact with a powerful woman associated with the northern pirate world.

Their relationship remains one of the most mysterious aspects of his personal history.

Whatever transpired between them continued to influence Grath long after he abandoned his former life.

### The Liberation of Port Llast

Approximately thirty-five years before the events of the campaign, Port Llast was under pirate occupation.

During this turbulent period, Grath took part in the effort to free the settlement.

His involvement proved important enough that the town eventually recognized him with the title of First Captain.

The position carried both political authority and responsibility for the settlement's protection.

Grath's actions during the liberation established his reputation among the inhabitants of Port Llast.

To many residents, he was not merely a former pirate but a man who had turned against the lawlessness of his previous life and helped restore their freedom.

The precise events of the liberation, the identities of the occupying pirates, and the circumstances of Grath's decision to fight them have not been fully recorded.

### Becoming First Captain

Following the liberation, Grath remained in Port Llast.

Over the following decades, he became an established figure in the settlement's administration.

As First Captain, he assumed responsibilities comparable to those of a mayor, overseeing civic matters and representing the town's interests.

His leadership style is practical and direct.

Rather than relying upon elaborate political ceremony, Grath approaches problems with the experience of someone accustomed to making difficult decisions under pressure.

The inhabitants generally respect his authority, although his reserved manner and unwillingness to discuss certain subjects have contributed to an air of mystery around him.

### A Life Left Behind

Despite decades spent governing Port Llast, Grath has never entirely escaped his maritime past.

His home contains objects and correspondence that connect him to his former life.

Among them are old pirate relics, sea charts, a peculiar compass, and paintings depicting an unidentified woman.

The continued presence of these possessions suggests that Grath has not completely severed his emotional ties to the sea.

Whether he remains in contact with individuals from his past is unknown.

## History in The Daughter of the Moon

### Meeting the Adventurers

Grath first appeared during the adventuring party's investigation of Port Llast in Saga I, Session 2.

The party, consisting of Bramwell Elixor, Luna Hale, Björn Bloodspiller, and Fenwick Elderbranch, had traveled to the settlement after receiving an invitation from Jimsko.

Their initial objective was to investigate unusual behavior surrounding the town's lighthouse.

During a visit to the docks, the adventurers encountered Grath and delivered a letter into his hands.

His reaction was noticeably uncomfortable.

Rather than providing the straightforward response the adventurers expected, Grath appeared evasive and increasingly suspicious.

The meeting caused the party to question whether the First Captain knew more about the disturbances than he was willing to reveal.

However, Grath had not instructed the adventurers to investigate the lighthouse. That request had originated with Jimsko.

### Suspicion and the Lighthouse

As the investigation continued, the adventurers learned of suspicious maritime activity and the possible existence of a false lighthouse.

The combination of these discoveries and Grath's behavior led the group to suspect that the town's leadership might be connected to the disturbances.

His maritime experience and responsibility for the settlement made him an obvious person of interest.

Rather than directly confronting the First Captain, the adventurers decided to investigate his residence.

### The Break-In

The party devised a distraction involving a seagull, which allowed them to gain access to Grath's home without permission.

Inside, they discovered numerous objects that raised further questions.

Among the most unusual were several paintings depicting the same unidentified woman overlooking the harbor.

The paintings showed her from different perspectives, creating a strange impression that the scene was being viewed across shifting moments in time.

The adventurers also discovered lighthouse keys, maritime documents, an old book associated with Selûne, and correspondence containing cryptic references to the sea.

Some of the messages appeared to urge Grath to return to the life he had left behind.

His possessions also included a peculiar compass, marked charts of the Sword Coast, and relics connected to piracy.

Taken together, these objects suggested that Grath possessed a considerably more complicated history than his public position indicated.

### The Shipment Records

While searching the residence, the adventurers were interrupted by a group of hired thieves.

The intruders appeared to be searching for shipment records.

The sudden confrontation forced the adventurers into combat.

Although they defeated most of the attackers, one escaped.

The incident demonstrated that the party was not alone in seeking information hidden within the First Captain's home.

Someone else had an interest in records connected to Port Llast's maritime activities.

However, the identity of the person who hired the thieves was not established.

Nor was it proven that Grath had knowingly participated in the operation that brought the intruders to his residence.

### The Lighthouse Conspiracy

Following the break-in, the adventurers continued their investigation of the lighthouse.

There, they encountered hostile shades, discovered an ancient shrine dedicated to Selûne, and confronted a bandit and two cultists performing a ritual involving a magical shard.

The ritual was interrupted, and the party recovered the artifact.

The shard demonstrated the ability to interfere with memories when Björn touched it.

The events confirmed that a genuine magical conspiracy was operating around Port Llast.

However, the discoveries did not establish Grath as one of its participants.

His suspicious behavior and concealed past remained separate mysteries.

## Personality

Grath is stern, pragmatic, guarded, and accustomed to authority.

His experiences as a sailor and former pirate have given him a practical understanding of danger and human nature.

He is not easily impressed, and he has little patience for unnecessary theatrics.

However, his reserved demeanor should not be mistaken for cruelty.

Having participated in Port Llast's liberation, Grath has demonstrated a willingness to protect others and confront dangerous forces when necessary.

He carries himself as a leader who believes actions are more important than promises.

Grath is also deeply private.

He rarely volunteers information about his earlier life, particularly when conversations approach matters connected to the sea and the people he once knew.

His evasiveness has occasionally made him appear untrustworthy, even when there is no evidence that he has committed wrongdoing.

Much of his characterization revolves around the contrast between the responsible leader he has become and the pirate he once was.

## The Mystery of the Woman

Perhaps the most unusual detail discovered within Grath's residence was his collection of paintings depicting an unidentified woman.

Each portrayed the same figure overlooking the harbor, but from a different perspective.

The paintings appeared to hold considerable personal significance.

Combined with the old letters and references to returning to the sea, they suggested an unresolved relationship from Grath's earlier life.

Grath is known to have a complicated history involving a powerful woman from the northern pirate world.

The full nature of their relationship has not been revealed.

Whether the woman depicted in the paintings is the same individual remains unconfirmed.

It is also unclear whether the paintings possess any magical qualities or whether their unusual perspectives are purely artistic.

For the adventurers, the discovery became one of several unanswered questions surrounding the First Captain.

## Relationships

### The People of Port Llast

Grath's most important public relationship is with the settlement he governs.

His reputation was established during the liberation of Port Llast, and the inhabitants have since entrusted him with considerable authority.

Although stern and occasionally difficult to approach, he is generally regarded as an experienced protector of the town.

### The Mysterious Pirate Woman

An important figure from Grath's former life remains connected to his personal history.

She is associated with the northern pirate world and appears to have left a lasting impression upon him.

Their past relationship, eventual separation, and present circumstances remain unresolved.

### Jimsko

Jimsko is a prominent dwarven resident of Port Llast whose concerns about the lighthouse brought the adventuring party to town.

Both men have an interest in the settlement's safety, although their methods and personalities differ.

Their precise personal relationship has not been fully established.

### The Adventuring Party

Grath encountered the original party during its investigation of Port Llast.

His uncomfortable response to their letter and the discoveries within his residence caused the adventurers to regard him with suspicion.

Nevertheless, the party never conclusively established that he was responsible for the lighthouse conspiracy.

His relationship with the adventurers remains complicated by the fact that they secretly entered and searched his home.

## Possessions

### The Maritime Paintings

A collection of portraits depicting the same mysterious woman overlooking Port Llast's harbor.

Their personal significance to Grath appears considerable, although their precise origins remain unknown.

### The Sea-Pointing Compass

An unusual compass kept among Grath's maritime possessions.

Its behavior and purpose have not been fully explained.

### Sword Coast Charts

Maps and maritime charts marked with locations along the northern Sword Coast.

These objects reflect Grath's familiarity with the region and its shipping routes.

### Pirate Relics

Various objects preserved from his former life at sea.

They serve as reminders of the years he spent outside the law and the people he once encountered.

### Lighthouse Keys

Keys granting access to areas associated with Port Llast's lighthouse.

Their discovery contributed to the adventurers' suspicions during the initial investigation.

### Old Correspondence

Letters and notes associated with Grath's past.

Some contain cryptic references encouraging him to return to the sea, suggesting that his former life continues to exert an influence over him.

## Notable Events

- Served as a pirate before settling in Port Llast.
- Participated in the liberation of the settlement approximately thirty-five years before Saga I.
- Earned the title of First Captain.
- Governed Port Llast for many years.
- Met the adventuring party during its investigation into the lighthouse.
- Reacted suspiciously when presented with a letter at the docks.
- Had his residence infiltrated and searched by the adventurers.
- Was found to possess mysterious maritime paintings, old correspondence, and lighthouse keys.
- Became indirectly involved in a confrontation between the adventurers and thieves seeking shipment records.
- Remained an object of suspicion despite the party discovering the cultist operation at the lighthouse.

## Trivia

- Grath is fifty-eight years old during the campaign.
- He was approximately twenty-three when Port Llast was liberated, based on the established chronology.
- His title of First Captain was earned through service rather than inheritance.
- Despite his responsibilities as a civic leader, he previously lived as a pirate.
- His residence contains several paintings of the same mysterious woman.
- He retains items associated with his past life at sea.
- The party initially suspected him of involvement in the lighthouse conspiracy.
- Grath was never established as a follower of Shar.
- His history with the northern pirate world remains unresolved.
- His name is shared with the historical founder associated with Port Llast's earliest history; the two should not be confused.

## Legacy and Significance

Grath Erlkar represents a different kind of mystery within *The Daughter of the Moon*.

Unlike the cultists operating beneath Port Llast, his secrets are not necessarily connected to forbidden magic, ancient prophecy, or religious fanaticism.

Instead, they belong to a man attempting to live beyond the choices of his youth.

Once a pirate, Grath helped liberate a town and eventually became its protector.

Yet his transformation from outlaw to leader did not erase the people, relationships, or memories he left behind.

To the adventurers, Grath initially appeared to be a potentially corrupt official hiding evidence of a dangerous conspiracy.

What they uncovered suggested a more complicated story.

Behind the First Captain's stern exterior lies a past that continues to haunt him, embodied by old letters, forgotten charts, and the portrait of a woman looking out toward the sea.

His story remains unfinished.

**Grath Erlkar may have left the sea behind, but the sea has not entirely let go of him.**
