Bandits, wild animals, and hostile creatures sometimes threaten those traveling without protection.

The original adventuring party traveled the northern Sword Coast's roads during its journey toward Port Llast.

### Maritime Trade

The Sea of Swords provides an alternative to overland travel.

Large merchant vessels transport goods between ports, allowing trade to continue even when inland routes become unsafe.

However, ships must contend with storms, pirates, hidden reefs, and dangerous coastal waters.

The importance of navigational beacons makes lighthouses especially valuable to maritime communities.

The lighthouse disturbances near Port Llast demonstrated how easily these structures could become instruments of danger rather than protection.

## Religion and Divine Influence

Religion plays a major role throughout the Sword Coast.

Numerous gods are worshipped by its inhabitants, and religious institutions often possess considerable social and political influence.

### Selûne — The Moonmaiden

Selûne is the goddess of the moon, stars, navigation, and those who travel beneath the night sky.

Her worship is particularly meaningful to sailors and travelers who depend upon celestial guidance.

Ancient shrines and temples dedicated to Selûne can be found throughout Faerûn.

During the campaign, the adventurers discovered a forgotten shrine beneath the Port Llast Lighthouse.

The discovery became one of the earliest connections between the party and the ancient prophecy.

Selûne is also central to the conflict involving Princess Yulia and the mysterious daughters described in the scroll.

### Shar — The Lady of Loss

Shar is the goddess of darkness, loss, secrets, and forgetfulness.

Her followers seek comfort in oblivion and often regard painful memories as burdens from which mortals should be freed.

Shar's opposition to Selûne is among the oldest divine conflicts in the Forgotten Realms.

During *The Daughter of the Moon*, individuals associated with Shar became involved in the search for the ancient prophetic scroll.

Their activities eventually connected the party's investigations in Port Llast to the greater mysteries of Luskan and the Moonfall Vault.

### Mystra — The Goddess of Magic

Mystra governs the Weave, the magical force through which most spellcasters access arcane power.

Her influence is fundamental to the practice of magic throughout Faerûn.

The adventurers encountered references to Mystra and the origins of the Weave during their investigations into ancient Netherese writings.

These discoveries suggested that the prophetic scroll belonged to a magical tradition with roots far older than the present political powers of the Sword Coast.

### Helm — The Watcher

Helm is the god of vigilance, duty, and protection.

His followers emphasize responsibility, discipline, and the defense of those entrusted to their care.

Bramwell Elixor, one of the original adventurers, is a cleric of Helm.

His faith and personal history became important aspects of the party's adventures, particularly when his actions brought him into conflict with religious authorities.

## History in The Daughter of the Moon

### The Beginning — Port Llast

The recorded events of Saga I began when four travelers met along the road to Port Llast.

Bramwell Elixor, Luna Hale, Björn Bloodspiller, and Fenwick Elderbranch agreed to travel together after discovering they shared the same destination.

Upon reaching Port Llast, they met Jimsko, who asked them to investigate suspicious disturbances surrounding the town's lighthouse.

The adventurers soon discovered that the lighthouse concealed an ancient shrine dedicated to Selûne.

At its summit, they confronted cultists performing a ritual involving a mysterious magical shard.

When Björn touched the recovered artifact, his memories briefly disappeared.

The encounter provided the party's first experience with the strange magic that would become central to the unfolding story.

### The Pirate Conspiracy

Following the lighthouse investigation, the adventurers followed information concerning stolen scrolls and suspicious maritime activity.

Their search led to a pirate encampment hidden along the coast.

There they discovered a false lighthouse system and the entrance to the Caverns of Lior.

Deep within the caves, the party recovered an ancient magical scroll bearing a mysterious countdown.

They also confronted Velka, a woman involved in the operation surrounding the artifact.

The party defeated her and took her prisoner.

However, upon returning to Port Llast, they discovered that Jimsko had been abducted.

Evidence pointed north toward Luskan.

### The Prophecy of the Two Daughters

Shortly after Jimsko's disappearance, the adventurers encountered El, a woman belonging to an order devoted to Selûne.

She warned that the scroll's writing was disappearing and that its contents might soon be lost forever.

The party chose to travel toward Neverwinter to investigate the prophecy before pursuing Jimsko.

Within the city's library, a scholar helped translate the first portions of the ancient text.

Among the revealed fragments were:

*When the sea forgets the moon.*

*Two daughters shall walk beneath divided skies.*

The translation disrupted the magical countdown, allowing the party to preserve the remaining writing.

However, the meaning of the prophecy remained unclear.

### The Escape of Princess Yulia

During their departure from Neverwinter, the adventurers encountered Princess Yulia being escorted by guards.

The party intervened and helped the princess escape.

Yulia subsequently asked to accompany them.

Björn accepted responsibility for protecting her.

When the group attempted to travel through Neverwinter Woods, El arrived with guards.

Björn confronted the pursuers, allowing the others to escape.

He was captured, bringing his journey with the party to an abrupt end.

During the group's continued travels through the forest, they encountered Amel, a rogue who subsequently joined them.

### The Search in Luskan

The adventurers eventually arrived in Luskan seeking answers concerning Jimsko, the prophetic scroll, and the growing influence of Shar's followers.

Their investigations brought them into conflict with the Pirate Queen of the North.

The Queen sought information concerning a mysterious ancient location.

The party eventually discovered Jimsko and Velka imprisoned within one of her Ledger Houses.

After rescuing them, the adventurers learned of the Moonfall Vault, a hidden site beneath the sea.

The Queen revealed that she had manipulated the rescue to obtain the information she desired.

The race toward the ancient vault had begun.

### The Moonfall Vault

Following their escape from Luskan, the adventurers returned briefly to Port Llast.

There, Jimsko collected his belongings while the party prepared for a dangerous expedition.

Princess Yulia, Velka, and Vesper remained behind to investigate related mysteries on land.

The remaining adventurers departed by ship toward the Moonfall Vault.

Their journey eventually brought them to an ancient island sanctuary dedicated to Selûne.

A magical moon pool opened a passage into a submerged complex filled with ruins, dangerous creatures, and forgotten magic.

After overcoming the monstrous Crab Queen and recovering a magical orb, the party activated another ancient mechanism.

Their actions revealed a corrupted statue of Selûne and a terrifying elder lich.

The creature unleashed a powerful spell that cast the adventurers into the Shadowfell.

### Beyond the Sword Coast

The adventurers' journey continued within the Shadowfell, where they explored Blackreach and eventually discovered the Keeper.

With the Keeper's assistance, they opened a Shadow Crossing and escaped the realm.

However, their return did not bring them back to the Sword Coast.

Instead, they emerged unconscious in a distant wheat field, far from the lands where their journey began.

Their subsequent travels toward Kestrel Ford and Thamor marked the beginning of Saga II.

Although the adventurers had left the Sword Coast behind, the mysteries of its northern cities, the prophetic scroll, and the daughters of Selûne and Shar remained unresolved.

## Notable Organizations and Powers

Several organizations influence the political and supernatural affairs of the Sword Coast.

**The Lords' Alliance:** A coalition of powerful settlements seeking stability, security, and cooperation throughout the region.

**The Harpers:** A secretive network devoted to opposing tyranny and preventing the abuse of powerful magic.

**The Emerald Enclave:** Defenders of the natural world who seek to preserve balance between civilization and wilderness.

**The Order of the Gauntlet:** A religious and martial alliance dedicated to confronting evil and protecting the innocent.

**The Zhentarim:** An influential network of mercenaries, merchants, and agents pursuing wealth and power.

**The Arcane Brotherhood:** A powerful organization of mages associated with Luskan.

**The Followers of Selûne:** Religious communities devoted to the Moonmaiden, including the order associated with El in the campaign.

**The Followers of Shar:** Secretive worshippers of the Lady of Loss whose activities are connected to the prophetic scroll and the wider divine conflict.

## Significance

The Sword Coast is a region defined by contrasts.

Prosperous cities stand beside dangerous wilderness. Ancient religious traditions coexist with political ambition. Merchants and pirates compete for the same waters, while powerful organizations struggle for influence over lands that have rarely accepted a single ruler.

For the adventurers of *The Daughter of the Moon*, the region was the birthplace of their story.

Its roads brought four strangers together.

Its forests tested their loyalty and compassion.

Its cities introduced them to political intrigue, divine prophecy, and the consequences of their decisions.

And beneath its seas, ancient magic carried them into a realm where memories themselves could be stolen.

Although their journey eventually led beyond the Sword Coast, the mysteries uncovered there continue to shape the unfolding campaign.

The prophecy remains only partially understood, the conflict between Selûne and Shar continues, and the fates of those left behind remain connected to the adventurers' larger destiny.

**For some, the Sword Coast is a land of trade and opportunity. For others, it is a dangerous frontier. But for the adventurers of The Daughter of the Moon, it is where an ordinary journey became a legend.**

pages.title: Kestrel Ford
pages.summary: A lively road village where the adventurers chose their name.
pages.body:
# The village at the ford
**Kestrel Ford** is a village on the journey toward [[Thamor]]. Its roads carry merchants, local news, and travelers with different reasons to hurry onward.

It was around this stage of their travels that the party took the name [[The Four Seasons]].

Here, ordinary village life briefly offered a contrast to the great affairs waiting in the city ahead.

pages.title: Thamor
pages.summary: A city of blue-and-gold banners, a child king, and uneasy celebrations.
pages.body:
# Under blue and gold
**Thamor** is a crowded city ruled by [[King Arven I]]. Visitors find lively streets, merchants, ceremony preparations, and the constant movement of a city hoping for a stable future.

## The crown and its rivals
Thamor's independence has drawn pressure from [[Mourktar]], while stories of the [[Dragon's Due]] have troubled its residents.

## A public gathering
At [[Crown Square]], the young king's knighting ceremony drew a large crowd and a formidable guard presence. [[The Four Seasons]] witnessed an attempted attack during the proceedings.

The party has also crossed paths with [[Cinder]] in the city.

pages.title: Crown Square
pages.summary: The ceremonial heart of Thamor and the setting of a memorable knighting.
pages.body:
# A square beneath the banners
**Crown Square** is a prominent public gathering place in [[Thamor]]. During [[King Arven I]]'s knighting ceremony, the square thronged with guards, nobles, townsfolk, and visiting spectators.

An arrow and the appearance of assailants cast a sudden shadow over the celebration. [[Bramwell Elixor]] was among those who reacted to the danger.

pages.title: Mourktar
pages.summary: A rival power whose dealings with Thamor have become a topic of concern.
pages.body:
# Beyond Thamor
**Mourktar** is a distant center of power mentioned in connection with [[Thamor]]'s political situation.

The city and its envoys are discussed in the context of competing claims, diplomatic pressure, and the future of [[King Arven I]]'s reign.

What these tensions mean for the adventurers remains to be seen.

pages.title: Blackreach
pages.summary: A place remembered from the party’s travels before they reached Kestrel Ford.
pages.body:
# A road behind them
**Blackreach** is a location in the recent travels of [[The Four Seasons]], before their arrival at [[Kestrel Ford]].

This is a short entry, ready to be expanded with player-confirmed recollections and discoveries.

pages.title: Selûne
pages.summary: The Moonmaiden, deity of moonlight, whose name threads through the campaign.
pages.body:
# The Moonmaiden
**Selûne**, the Moonmaiden, is a deity associated with the moon, guiding light, and those who seek their way through darkness.

A shrine beneath the [[Port Llast Lighthouse]] and the discovery of the [[Moon Scroll]] drew the attention of [[The Four Seasons]] to the goddess and her history.

Selûne's ancient opposition to [[Shar]] lies at the heart of many stories in the world.

pages.title: Shar
pages.summary: The Lady of Loss, a deity associated with darkness and secrets.
pages.body:
# The Lady of Loss
**Shar** is a deity often associated with darkness, loss, and hidden things.

Her legendary conflict with [[Selûne]] is known far beyond temples and ancient manuscripts. The [[Moon Scroll]] has brought echoes of that conflict close to [[The Four Seasons]].

Much remains unknown about what this history may mean for the present.

pages.title: Helm
pages.summary: The Watcher, god of guardians, duty, and vigilance.
pages.body:
# The Watcher
**Helm** is the god of watchfulness and guardianship, revered by those sworn to stand between danger and the people they protect.

[[Bramwell Elixor]] serves Helm as a cleric, although questions of doctrine and duty have not always led him down the easiest path.

pages.title: Moon Scroll
pages.summary: An ancient scroll whose discovery changed the direction of the party’s journey.
pages.body:
# A recovered mystery
The **Moon Scroll** is an ancient document recovered during the early adventures of [[The Four Seasons]]. The party's investigation of the [[Port Llast Lighthouse]] and [[Caverns of Lior]] placed the scroll at the center of their journey.

The writing has been connected with ancient Netherese language and with the histories of [[Selûne]] and [[Shar]].

## What remains unknown
Its full implications are not yet part of the public chronicle. This entry records only what the travelers have learned.

pages.title: Dragon's Due
pages.summary: An ominous obligation discussed in connection with Thamor and a red dragon.
pages.body:
# A shadow over the city
The phrase **Dragon's Due** is spoken around [[Thamor]] as a source of apprehension.

It is associated with reports of a powerful red dragon and concerns over the city's security and autonomy. Political tensions involving [[Mourktar]] have only increased uncertainty.

How much is rumor, how much is threat, and how much is politics remains to be discovered by [[The Four Seasons]].

pages.title: How to Use This Wiki
pages.summary: A quick introduction to browsing and contributing to the living campaign encyclopedia.
pages.body:
# Welcome to the Living Atlas
**Daughter of the Moon Wiki** is a player-safe encyclopedia of people, places, and adventures of [[The Four Seasons]].

## Explore
- **World Atlas**: switch between the Sword Coast, Threskel, and the Shadowfell. Click a pin to open the location and its session appearances. Maps are schematic, not precise geography.
- **Connections**: focus any wiki article to see the constellation of related people, organizations, locations, and artifacts.
- **Session Journal**: open each recap or add your own next session.
- **Quest Board**: starts empty. Post a quest during a session and mark it Open, In progress, Completed, or Archived.

## Edit articles and add artwork
Use **Edit this article** or **New entry** to change text, upload a cover or gallery portraits, and add rich internal references such as `[[Neverwinter]]` or `[[Neverwinter|the city]]`. A character gallery is made of images added through the scribe's editor.

## Draw your own routes and links
On the **World Atlas**, choose *Edit map & routes* to add pins for existing articles, position them by coordinates, and create routes. Choose *Move pins* to drag them directly. On **Connections**, use *Edit relationships* to add or remove links between any two entries.

## Publish carefully
Edits save to your browser first, including drafts, quests, map changes, relationships, and session text. Choose **Edit wiki** → **Publish to GitHub** with a repository-scoped editor token when you're ready for players to see them. Other readers don't need any token. Don't paste tokens into content.

**Backups matter:** the editor's Download complete backup command includes images that haven't been published yet. On another browser/device, restore that backup before continuing.

## Player-safe by design
There is no password-protected DM section. Unrevealed plans and backstories must remain outside this public GitHub repository.

pages.title: Neverwinter Woods
pages.summary: A wilderness of hidden paths, an old druid sanctuary, and unlikely meetings.
pages.body:
# Neverwinter Woods

*The Ancient Forest of the Sword Coast*

**Also known as:** Neverwinter Wood, Llewyrrwood  

**Location:** Sword Coast North, Faerûn  

**Region:** East and northeast of Neverwinter  

**Type:** Ancient, magically influenced forest  

**Nearby locations:** Neverwinter, Mount Hotenow, Luskan, Neverwinter River  

**Religious associations:** Silvanus, druidic traditions  

**Known inhabitants:** Druids, wolves, giant spiders, owlbears, blood hawks, mysterious woodland creatures  

**Notable landmarks:** Statue of Silvanus, Hidden Druid Sanctuary, Guardian's Cavern
 
**Campaign appearance:** Saga I, Sessions 6–7  

**Status:** Existing; much of the woodland remains unexplored

---

## Overview

Neverwinter Woods is an ancient and sprawling forest in the northern Sword Coast, stretching across the wilderness east of the city of Neverwinter. Known for its dense woodland, hidden ruins, powerful natural magic, and unusual inhabitants, the forest has long been a place of mystery to travelers and scholars alike.

The woods possess a strange, almost watchful atmosphere. Ancient trees tower over winding paths, wildlife flourishes far from civilization, and forgotten sites lie concealed beneath roots and stone.

The forest is particularly important to druids and followers of nature deities, including Silvanus, the Oak Father. Hidden deep within its wilderness are sacred places protected by powerful creatures and ancient enchantments.

During the events of *The Daughter of the Moon*, Neverwinter Woods became a crucial location in the adventuring party's journey north.

It was here that Björn Bloodspiller sacrificed his freedom to protect Princess Yulia, the rogue Amel joined the adventurers, and Fenwick Elderbranch discovered a hidden druid sanctuary.

The party also encountered mysterious signs of supernatural activity, including animals exhibiting unusual intelligence and a moonlit creature whose apparent interest in Princess Yulia hinted at a connection to the unfolding prophecy.

## Geography and Environment

Neverwinter Woods occupies a large region of wilderness surrounding the eastern approaches to Neverwinter.

The forest is characterized by thick woodland, winding streams, overgrown trails, rocky outcroppings, and secluded clearings.

The Neverwinter River flows through the region from Mount Hotenow, a volcanic mountain whose supernatural heat contributes to the unusually warm waters associated with the city of Neverwinter.

Despite the forest's proximity to a major city, its deeper reaches remain largely untouched by ordinary settlement.

Travelers unfamiliar with the woodland can easily become lost among its winding paths, particularly when attempting to avoid established roads.

Some regions possess an unmistakable magical atmosphere. Ancient shrines, unusual animal behavior, and hidden passages suggest that the forest holds secrets considerably older than the kingdoms surrounding it.

### Ancient History

Long before the present age, the forest was associated with the elves of Illefarn, who referred to it as Llewyrrwood.

Remnants of ancient civilizations and forgotten magical traditions remain scattered throughout the wider woodland.

In the centuries since, the forest has sheltered druids, dangerous beasts, fey creatures, and those wishing to live beyond the influence of major settlements.

Its wilderness has also attracted adventurers, treasure hunters, and scholars seeking evidence of civilizations lost to time.

## Notable Locations

### The Statue of Silvanus

Deep within the forest stands an ancient statue dedicated to Silvanus, the Oak Father and god of wild nature.

During the adventurers' journey, the statue became an important landmark in their search for a hidden druid sanctuary.

The party encountered a mysterious crow near the monument. Rather than behaving like an ordinary bird, the creature whispered directions toward a concealed forest path.

The encounter suggested that the forest's guardians were aware of the adventurers' presence and were guiding them toward an important destination.

### The Hidden Forest Path

The pathway leading toward the druid sanctuary is concealed within the deeper wilderness.

Its location is not immediately apparent to travelers, and the party only discovered it after following clues connected to the statue of Silvanus.

The path led the adventurers through dangerous woodland inhabited by hostile creatures before eventually reaching a cave marked with ancient druidic writing.

### The Guardian's Cavern

The entrance to the hidden sanctuary lies within an ancient cavern protected by natural and magical obstacles.

Near its entrance, the adventurers discovered an inscription warning that only those considered pure could enter.

The cavern's interior contained glowing crystals, dangerous giant spiders, and an enormous owlbear guarding a sealed stone door.

The owlbear served as the final obstacle separating outsiders from the sanctuary beyond.

Unknown to most travelers, the guardian was also part of a test of character.

An inscription on the sealed door read:

*Hurt not the Guardian and you shall pass.*

Those who harmed the guardian were unable to open the passage through ordinary means.

Only Fenwick Elderbranch, who had refused to attack the owlbear, succeeded in opening the door.

### The Hidden Druid Sanctuary

Beyond the sealed entrance lies a secluded sanctuary maintained by druids devoted to the natural world.

The sanctuary is an ancient refuge hidden from ordinary travelers and protected by the surrounding forest.

Its inhabitants maintain traditions centered on the preservation of nature, respect for living creatures, and the balance between civilization and the wilderness.

The adventurers gained entry after Fenwick passed the guardian's test.

Inside, Fenwick received a distinctive serpent-shaped druidic staff.

The sanctuary also became associated with further mysteries surrounding the party, including unusual natural magic and a supernatural encounter involving Princess Yulia.

## History in The Daughter of the Moon

### The Escape from Neverwinter

Following their investigations in Neverwinter, the adventuring party helped Princess Yulia escape from her royal escort.

The princess expressed a desire to accompany the adventurers rather than return to the restrictions of royal life.

Seeking to avoid unwanted attention, the group chose to travel through Neverwinter Woods instead of following the main roads.

Their journey was interrupted near the outskirts of the forest when El arrived with two guards.

Björn Bloodspiller, who had promised to protect Princess Yulia, deliberately revealed himself to confront the pursuers.

Although his actions placed him in immediate danger, they provided the remaining adventurers with an opportunity to escape.

Björn was restrained and captured.

The others fled deeper into the forest with Princess Yulia, leaving their companion behind.

For the party, the incident marked a painful turning point.

Their journey through Neverwinter Woods had begun with the loss of one of their founding members.

### The Encounter with Amel

While traveling deeper into the forest, the adventurers discovered signs of a struggle.

Following the disturbance, they encountered a rogue named Amel, who was fighting a flock of aggressive blood hawks.

The party intervened and helped him survive the encounter.

Amel revealed that he was also attempting to reach Luskan, though he had become hopelessly lost in the surrounding wilderness.

Recognizing that they shared a destination, the adventurers agreed to travel together.

Amel subsequently joined the group, marking the beginning of his involvement in the wider events of the campaign.

His arrival followed closely upon Björn's capture, changing the composition of the adventuring party.

### The Meeting with Volo

During their travels, the adventurers encountered the eccentric storyteller and renowned traveler Volothamp Geddarm, commonly known as Volo.

The meeting introduced the party to rumors concerning a hidden druid sanctuary somewhere within the forest.

Intrigued by the possibility of discovering such a place, particularly Fenwick, the group began seeking evidence of its existence.

Volo's information helped direct their attention toward the ancient mysteries concealed within the woodland.

### The Watchful Wolf

As the party continued its journey, Fenwick noticed an unusual wolf observing them from a distance.

The animal did not behave like an ordinary predator.

Rather than attack, it watched the adventurers and remained elusive.

Its behavior suggested intelligence or purpose beyond that normally expected of a wild creature.

Fenwick began to suspect that another druid might be nearby, possibly observing the group through an animal form.

The wolf's true nature was not immediately established.

### Brick's Mysterious Voice

Around the same time, Brick, the party's crab companion, reported hearing a strange voice within his mind.

The source of the voice remained uncertain.

Combined with the watching wolf and other unusual phenomena, the experience reinforced the impression that the party was being observed by forces they did not understand.

Whether the voice originated from a druid, a forest spirit, or another supernatural presence was not determined.

### Discovery of the Sanctuary

After encountering the statue of Silvanus and following the directions of a mysterious crow, the adventurers discovered the hidden route leading toward the druid sanctuary.

Their journey brought them into conflict with hostile forest creatures before they reached a cavern bearing ancient druidic inscriptions.

Inside, the group faced giant spiders and eventually encountered an owlbear guarding a sealed passage.

The situation deteriorated when one of Bramwell's attacks accidentally destroyed the creature's egg.

Enraged, the owlbear attacked.

The adventurers fought and ultimately killed the creature.

Fenwick, however, refused to harm it.

After the battle, the party discovered that the sanctuary's entrance was protected by a test of restraint.

Because Fenwick had not attacked the guardian, the sealed door opened when he touched it.

His companions were able to follow him into the sanctuary.

The encounter became a significant moment in Fenwick's personal journey, affirming the importance of compassion within his druidic beliefs.

### The Druids and the Moonlit Creature

Within the hidden sanctuary, the party encountered druids and explored a place largely untouched by the outside world.

Fenwick was particularly interested in its traditions and received a serpent-shaped staff during the visit.

The group also encountered unusual magical phenomena connected to the natural world.

Bramwell discovered a strange plant, and a subsequent magical occurrence involving a glowing book brought forth a mysterious moonlit creature.

The creature appeared to take a particular interest in Princess Yulia.

Its behavior suggested that the princess possessed some significance beyond what her companions fully understood.

At the time, the adventurers could only speculate about the meaning of the encounter and its possible connection to the divine mysteries surrounding their journey.

### Departure Toward Luskan

After exploring the sanctuary, the party continued traveling through the forest toward Luskan.

Their departure was not entirely uneventful, and the group suffered the loss of its cart during the journey.

Eventually, they emerged from the wilderness and continued toward the dangerous City of Sails.

Their time in Neverwinter Woods had fundamentally altered the party.

Björn was gone, Amel had joined them, Fenwick had discovered an important druidic refuge, and Princess Yulia had become associated with increasingly mysterious supernatural events.

## Flora and Fauna

Neverwinter Woods supports a wide variety of ordinary and magical wildlife.

Among creatures encountered or observed by the adventurers were wolves, blood hawks, giant spiders, and an owlbear.

Ordinary wildlife occasionally displayed behavior suggesting supernatural influence, including a watchful wolf and a crow capable of communicating directions.

The forest also contains ancient trees, dense undergrowth, unusual plants, and magically illuminated caverns.

Its relationship with druidic traditions suggests that not every creature within the woods should be regarded as an enemy.

Some may be guardians, messengers, or participants in ancient natural rituals.

## Magic and Religious Significance

### Silvanus and the Balance of Nature

Silvanus is one of the principal deities associated with the forest's druidic traditions.

The statue encountered by the adventurers demonstrates the Oak Father's religious importance within the region.

The hidden sanctuary's guardian trial reflects an understanding of nature centered on restraint and respect.

Those seeking entry were tested not merely on strength, but on their willingness to avoid unnecessary harm.

### The Moonlit Mystery

The appearance of a mysterious moonlit creature during the party's visit suggested that the forest might also contain magical forces associated with the moon.

Its apparent recognition of Princess Yulia raised questions about her significance in the unfolding prophecy.

However, the creature's precise nature and intentions remain uncertain.

## Known Individuals Associated with the Forest

**Fenwick Elderbranch:** A gnome druid who discovered and gained access to the hidden sanctuary by refusing to harm its guardian.

**Princess Yulia:** The princess of Neverwinter, whose escape led the party into the forest and whose presence attracted the attention of a mysterious moonlit creature.

**Björn Bloodspiller:** A founding member of the adventuring party who was captured while protecting Yulia near the forest's outskirts.

**Amel:** A rogue encountered fighting blood hawks. He joined the adventurers during their journey through the woodland.

**Volo:** A wandering storyteller and traveler who informed the party about the hidden druid sanctuary.

**Bramwell Elixor:** A cleric of Helm whose actions during the owlbear encounter had unintended consequences.

**Luna Hale:** A founding member of the party who traveled through the woods following Princess Yulia's escape.

## Notable Events

- The adventurers fled Neverwinter with Princess Yulia.
- Björn Bloodspiller was captured after confronting El and two guards.
- The party rescued Amel from blood hawks.
- Volo informed the adventurers about a hidden druid sanctuary.
- Fenwick observed a mysterious wolf following the group.
- Brick reported hearing a voice within his mind.
- A crow guided the party from a statue of Silvanus toward a hidden path.
- The adventurers discovered the Guardian's Cavern.
- Fenwick passed the sanctuary's test by refusing to harm the owlbear.
- The party encountered druids and obtained new knowledge and equipment.
- A mysterious moonlit creature appeared and showed interest in Princess Yulia.
- The adventurers continued onward toward Luskan.

## Significance

Neverwinter Woods represents one of the most important transitional locations in the early events of *The Daughter of the Moon*.

For the adventuring party, the forest was simultaneously a refuge, a place of loss, and a source of discovery.

It offered sanctuary from those pursuing Princess Yulia, but only after Björn sacrificed his freedom.

It introduced the rogue Amel, who would become an important companion during the later adventures.

It provided Fenwick with an opportunity to demonstrate the values that defined his relationship with nature.

And it offered further evidence that mysterious powers were taking an interest in Princess Yulia.

Although the adventurers eventually left the forest behind, its events continued to influence their journey toward Luskan, the Moonfall Vault, and the Shadowfell.

**Neverwinter Woods remains a place where the wilderness guards its secrets, and where those who seek passage may discover that mercy carries greater power than violence.**

pages.title: Druid Sanctuary
pages.summary: A secluded refuge found beyond a cavern guarded by an owlbear.
pages.body:
A crow near a statue of Silvanus pointed the party toward a hidden route through [[Neverwinter Wood]]. Past spiders and an owlbear, [[Fenwick]] entered a sanctuary accessible to those who had spared its guardian.

[[Saga I — Session 6: Into the Woods]] and [[Saga I — Session 7: Road to Luskan]] recount the visit.

pages.title: Flynn's Safehouse
pages.summary: A refuge and meeting place for the party during their time in Luskan.
pages.body:
After meeting [[Flynn]] at a performance in [[Luskan]], the adventurers found temporary shelter at his safehouse. They returned here while navigating the Pirate Queen's demands and the rescue of [[Jimsko]].

The house was eventually compromised. See [[Saga I — Session 10: The Ledger House]].

pages.title: The Ledger House
pages.summary: A suspicious Luskan property where an important rescue took place.
pages.body:
A supposed tax office in [[Luskan]] concealed imprisoned captives. The adventurers infiltrated it at night and rescued [[Jimsko]] and [[Velka]].

See [[Saga I — Session 10: The Ledger House]].

pages.title: Moonfall Island
pages.summary: A moonlit island whose ancient pool opened the way below the sea.
pages.body:
A ruined island and circular pool associated with [[Selûne]]. When the [[Moon Scroll]] was spoken under the moon, the waters opened into a portal toward the [[Moonfall Vault]].

See [[Saga I — Session 12: Beneath the Moon]].

pages.title: Moonfall Vault
pages.summary: A legendary underwater sanctuary reached through a moonlit portal.
pages.body:
[[Jimsko]] spoke of a hidden vault beneath the sea. The party set sail from [[Port Llast]] and reached a portal on [[Moonfall Island]], eventually entering a submerged sanctuary filled with ancient magic, strange creatures, and a ruined shrine of [[Selûne]].

Its depths led into an unexpected journey to the [[Shadowfell]].

pages.title: The Shadowfell
pages.summary: A shadowed plane of lost memories, illusions, and costly passage.
pages.body:
The party was cast into this bleak realm from the [[Moonfall Vault]]. They journeyed across black grass toward [[Blackreach]], where memories could serve as payment and a [[Shadow Crossing]] offered hope of a return home.

Follow the journey in [[Saga I — Session 13: The Shadowfell]] and beyond.

pages.title: Eye of Memories
pages.summary: A mysterious institution in Blackreach said to hold memories and clues to escape.
pages.body:
Within [[Blackreach]], the party sought the Eye of Memories and its priest in hopes of discovering the whereabouts of the [[Keeper]]. Its archive concerned lost memories and the last [[Shadow Crossing]].

See [[Saga I — Session 14: The Eye of Memories]].

pages.title: Forgotten District
pages.summary: A hidden passage beneath Blackreach leading to a remarkable encounter.
pages.body:
With [[Annabel]]'s help, the group entered a secret district under [[Blackreach]] and reached a vast door. Beyond it they finally met the [[Keeper]].

See [[Saga I — Session 17: The Unforgotten]].

pages.title: Crown of Embers
pages.summary: A Neverwinter tavern remembered for a night that descended into chaos.
pages.body:
Some of the party stayed here during their first time in [[Neverwinter]]. One evening's festivities escalated into a tavern-wide brawl.

See [[Saga I — Session 5: The Prophecy]].

pages.title: Wizard's Rest
pages.summary: A scholarly haven visited by Fenwick in Neverwinter.
pages.body: [[Fenwick]] spent an evening here while the rest of the adventurers went to the [[Crown of Embers]]. Later, the party pursued research into the [[Moon Scroll]].

pages.title: Thamor Stables
pages.summary: A stable near the busy streets of Thamor where the party left its horses.
pages.body: The Four Seasons arrived in [[Thamor]] and left their newly purchased mounts here before exploring the city. Crowds had gathered for [[King Arven I]]'s knighting ceremony in [[Crown Square]].

pages.title: Flynn
pages.summary: A resourceful Luskan contact rescued from the caves near Port Llast.
pages.body: The party freed [[Flynn]] from captivity during their first investigations near [[Port Llast]]. He later repaid the favor in [[Luskan]], supplying contacts and a temporary safehouse. He assisted with passage by ship toward the [[Moonfall Vault]].

pages.title: Amel
pages.summary: A quick-thinking adventurer who met the party in Neverwinter Wood.
pages.body:
[[Amel]] fought alongside the company after their encounter with blood hawks in [[Neverwinter Wood]]. He later traveled with them through [[Luskan]] and into the [[Shadowfell]].

He became part of the group's later Saga I history.

pages.title: Vesper
pages.summary: A young person encountered in Luskan who traveled with the company.
pages.body: The party met [[Vesper]] during its stay in [[Luskan]]. She later accompanied the others toward [[Port Llast]], where Vesper, [[Velka]], and [[Princess Yulia]] remained behind during the sea voyage.

pages.title: The Pirate Queen
pages.summary: A formidable power in Luskan who bargained with and manipulated the party.
pages.body:
In [[Luskan]], the adventurers were brought before a pirate queen who offered information and leverage involving [[Jimsko]] and [[Velka]]. The encounter led them to the [[Ledger House]].

Her interest in the [[Moonfall Vault]] placed her in rivalry with the group.

pages.title: Annabel
pages.summary: A lost memory in Blackreach who sought one last moment with her mother.
pages.body: In the [[Shadowfell]], the group met [[Annabel]], a child searching for her mother [[Ariana]]. After they helped reunite the pair, Annabel guided them toward the [[Forgotten District]] and the [[Keeper]].

pages.title: Ariana
pages.summary: Annabel’s mother, living in Blackreach with fading recollections.
pages.body: The adventurers visited [[Ariana]]'s home in [[Blackreach]]. With the help of a family portrait, they briefly restored her memory of her daughter [[Annabel]].

pages.title: The Keeper
pages.summary: An ancient presence the party met beneath Blackreach.
pages.body:
Deep in the [[Forgotten District]], the adventurers encountered the [[Keeper]]. It offered a chance to open a [[Shadow Crossing]], provided the company could protect it through a dangerous ritual.

The confrontation is recorded in [[Saga I — Session 17: The Unforgotten]].

pages.title: Verren
pages.summary: A powerful, enigmatic traveling companion whose path later diverged.
pages.body:
The mysterious wizard traveled with the company during the [[Shadowfell]] chapter and helped them return home. Later, after reaching the Material Plane, he departed to recover memories and regain control of his magic.

Names in the adventurers' retellings vary, including Veren and Varen.

pages.title: Cinder the Fairy
pages.summary: An animated healer introduced to the company in Thamor.
pages.body: The Four Seasons encountered [[Cinder]] in [[Thamor]] during preparations for the young king's ceremony. He was known for flamboyant behavior and healing magic.

pages.title: Lysa
pages.summary: A traveler helped by the company near Kestrel Ford.
pages.body: On their way toward [[Kestrel Ford]], the party helped [[Lysa]] after trouble involving goblins and a flock of sheep. The misadventure became one of the early stories of Saga II.

pages.title: Shadow Crossing
pages.summary: A rare passage between the Shadowfell and the Material Plane.
pages.body: During their stay in [[Blackreach]], the party learned of [[Shadow Crossing]]s that might provide a road home from the [[Shadowfell]]. The [[Keeper]] ultimately helped them open such a passage after they survived a difficult defense.

pages.title: Saga I — Session 1: The Road to Port Llast
pages.summary: Session 1 · Retold by Bramwell · The Road to Port Llast.
pages.body:
## The adventure

[[Bramwell Elixor]], [[Luna]], [[Bjorn]] and [[Fenwick]] met on the road to [[Port Llast]]. A wrecked merchant wagon, a thief and wolves tested the strangers before they encountered [[Jimsko]] at [[The Net & Keg]]. Rumors of a failing [[Port Llast Lighthouse]] drew their attention.

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 2: The Flickering Lighthouse
pages.summary: Session 2 · Retold by Fenwick · The Flickering Lighthouse.
pages.body:
## The adventure

At the docks the group met Port Llast’s mayor. With the help of [[Brick]], they investigated the mayor’s home, found a book concerning [[Selûne]], fought shades beneath the [[Port Llast Lighthouse]], and stopped a ritual involving a magical shard at the tower’s top.

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 3: The Hidden Cove
pages.summary: Session 3 · Retold by Bjorn · The Hidden Cove.
pages.body:
## The adventure

[[Estephan]] joined the company. They raided a pirate beach camp, destroyed a false lighthouse and entered the [[Caverns of Lior]]. [[Flynn]] was freed; beyond a rune-locked wall they recovered the [[Moon Scroll]], whose magical numbers appeared to count down.

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 4: The Price of a Scroll
pages.summary: Session 4 · Retold by Luna · The Price of a Scroll.
pages.body:
## The adventure

The party captured [[Velka]] in the [[Caverns of Lior]]. On returning to [[Port Llast]], they found [[The Net & Keg]] attacked and [[Jimsko]] missing. Faced with a dwindling countdown and warnings about the scroll, they chose to seek answers in [[Neverwinter]] first.

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 5: The Prophecy
pages.summary: Session 5 · Retold by Bramwell · The Prophecy.
pages.body:
## The adventure

On the road to [[Neverwinter]], the adventurers met the fairies [[Wiwi]] and Nini. In the city, research yielded fragments of the [[Moon Scroll]]’s prophecy, and the countdown ceased. The group then helped [[Princess Yulia]] escape an escort; she joined their travels.

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 6: Into the Woods
pages.summary: Session 6 · Retold by Fenwick · Into the Woods.
pages.body:
## The adventure

Leaving [[Neverwinter]] by forest paths, [[Bjorn]] stayed behind when guards arrived. In [[Neverwinter Wood]], the others rescued [[Amel]], met Volo and found a cavern leading to the [[Druid Sanctuary]] past a dangerous owlbear.

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 7: Road to Luskan
pages.summary: Session 7 · Retold by Amel · Road to Luskan.
pages.body:
## The adventure

The adventurers reached the [[Druid Sanctuary]] and continued north to [[Luskan]]. The city quickly introduced them to its thieves, bargains, rumors and new faces, including [[Vesper]].

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 8: A Play About Us
pages.summary: Session 8 · Retold by Luna · A Play About Us.
pages.body:
## The adventure

Wanted posters in [[Luskan]] accused the travelers of abducting [[Princess Yulia]]. They attended a theatrical parody of their own exploits, met [[Flynn]] there and received an invitation to speak privately. A masked director then confronted [[Bramwell Elixor]].

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 9: The Pirate Queen
pages.summary: Session 9 · Retold by Bramwell · The Pirate Queen.
pages.body:
## The adventure

An encounter after the play led to imprisonment in a dangerous mansion. The adventurers escaped their cells, found magical items and met [[The Pirate Queen]], who bargained over [[Velka]], [[Jimsko]] and her enemies in [[Luskan]].

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 10: The Ledger House
pages.summary: Session 10 · Retold by Fenwick · The Ledger House.
pages.body:
## The adventure

The party infiltrated the [[Ledger House]] and rescued both [[Velka]] and [[Jimsko]]. They learned of the [[Moonfall Vault]], but [[The Pirate Queen]] had been listening. With [[Flynn]]’s help, they prepared to sail away from [[Luskan]].

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 11: To Sea
pages.summary: Session 11 · Retold by Amel · To Sea.
pages.body:
## The adventure

The company returned to [[Port Llast]], then left [[Velka]], [[Vesper]] and [[Princess Yulia]] on land while setting sail. Strange sea creatures attacked their vessel as the party pursued the hidden [[Moonfall Vault]].

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 12: Beneath the Moon
pages.summary: Session 12 · Retold by Luna · Beneath the Moon.
pages.body:
## The adventure

A moonlit reading of the [[Moon Scroll]] opened the waters on [[Moonfall Island]]. The adventurers entered the [[Moonfall Vault]], fought the Crab Queen and activated a statue of [[Selûne]]. An elder lich appeared and cast them into the [[Shadowfell]].

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 13: The Shadowfell
pages.summary: Session 13 · Retold by Bramwell · The Shadowfell.
pages.body:
## The adventure

The company awakened in the bleak [[Shadowfell]] and crossed black fields to [[Blackreach]]. Entry required giving up a memory. Among the city’s illusions and unnerving merchants, the party began searching for a [[Shadow Crossing]].

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 14: The Eye of Memories
pages.summary: Session 14 · Retold by Fenwick · The Eye of Memories.
pages.body:
## The adventure

Seeking a route home in [[Blackreach]], the group visited the library and [[Eye of Memories]], learning of the mysterious [[Keeper]] and the last [[Shadow Crossing]]. The Eye released a hostile creature of stolen voices and memories.

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 15: A Missing Memory
pages.summary: Session 15 · Retold by Amel · A Missing Memory.
pages.body:
## The adventure

After surviving the battle at the [[Eye of Memories]], the party searched [[Blackreach]] for an escaped memory. Their investigation turned toward a girl seen earlier in the city, with new signs of strange magic and uncertain allies.

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 16: The Girl and the Knight
pages.summary: Session 16 · Retold by Luna · The Girl and the Knight.
pages.body:
## The adventure

The company found [[Annabel]] and learned she could guide them toward the [[Keeper]]. A confrontation with the Black Knight in [[Blackreach]] was abruptly ended by their powerful companion [[Verren]].

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga I — Session 17: The Unforgotten
pages.summary: Session 17 · Retold by The Company · The Unforgotten.
pages.body:
## The adventure

[[Annabel]] was briefly reunited with [[Ariana]] and showed the party the entrance to the [[Forgotten District]]. There they defended the [[Keeper]] from the Unforgotten while it opened a [[Shadow Crossing]]. They escaped the [[Shadowfell]] and awoke in a wheat field on the Material Plane.

## Continue exploring

[[Campaign Chronicle]] · [[The Four Seasons]]

pages.title: Saga II — A Name at the Ford
pages.summary: The company emerges from the Shadowfell and begins Saga II.
pages.body:
## At the table

After returning from the [[Shadowfell]], the travelers and [[Verren]] journeyed toward [[Kestrel Ford]]. Along the road they helped [[Lysa]], encountered goblins and a sheep-related misadventure, and eventually chose a name for their company: [[The Four Seasons]]. [[Verren]] later parted ways with the others to pursue his own recovery.

*This recap covers only events confirmed to have happened in play.*

pages.title: Saga II — A Crown in Thamor
pages.summary: The travelers attend the young king’s knighting.
pages.body:
## At the table

The Four Seasons traveled from [[Kestrel Ford]] to [[Thamor]], stabled their horses at the [[Thamor Stables]], met [[Cinder]], explored the city and attended [[King Arven I]]’s knighting ceremony in [[Crown Square]]. An arrow interrupted the proceedings; [[Bramwell Elixor]] intervened to block the attack. Further commotion surrounded the ceremony. This is the latest publicly recorded chapter of the party’s Saga II travels.

*This recap covers only events confirmed to have happened in play.*

quests.title: THE ASH-REED COURIER
quests.body:
GUILD JOB: THE ASH-REED COURIER / 240 GP TOTAL

Client: Merchants' Exchange, with a small reward supplement from the Guild. 

Location: Reedglass Fen, about two hours east of Thamor's outer orchards; walking route leads past old toll markers.

Objective: Find Dera Sol, an adult courier last seen taking a sealed tribute packet to a local healer called Auntie Veyra. Return Dera alive if possible; recover the packet, notes, or proof of what happened.


Why urgent: Several burned traders bought “dragonfire ward” charms from a seller tied to the fen. One wagon burned despite the charm. Locals say the marks on its axles were made by an actual red dragon.
